root.label: Deep Learning
root.summary: A comprehensive approach to Artificial Intelligence that allows computers to learn from experience and understand the world through a nested hierarchy of concepts.

ai_foundations.label: Artificial Intelligence Foundations
ai_foundations.summary: The conceptual basis of AI, transitioning from rule-based systems to machine learning and representation learning.

deep_learning_definition.label: Deep Learning Definition
deep_learning_definition.summary: An AI approach utilizing a hierarchy of concepts where complex concepts are built from simpler ones.

dl_fact_1.label: Hierarchy of Concepts
dl_fact_1.summary: Deep learning enables the computer to learn complicated concepts by building them out of simpler ones (p. 1).

dl_fact_2.label: Learning from Experience
dl_fact_2.summary: Avoids the need for human operators to formally specify all required knowledge by gathering it from experience (p. 1).

mlp_concept.label: Multilayer Perceptron (MLP)
mlp_concept.summary: A mathematical function mapping input values to output values, formed by composing many simpler functions (p. 5).

representation_learning.label: Representation Learning
representation_learning.summary: The process of using machine learning to discover the representation of data itself, rather than just the mapping from representation to output.

autoencoder_concept.label: Autoencoder
autoencoder_concept.summary: A combination of an encoder function (converting input to a different representation) and a decoder function (converting the representation back to original format) (p. 4).

factors_of_variation.label: Factors of Variation
factors_of_variation.summary: Separate sources of influence that explain observed data, often unobserved objects or forces in the physical world (p. 4).

disentanglement.label: Disentanglement
disentanglement.summary: The process of separating the factors of variation and discarding the ones that are irrelevant to the task (p. 4).

model_depth.label: Model Depth
model_depth.summary: Measurements of how 'deep' a model is, viewed from two primary perspectives.

depth_computational_graph.label: Computational Graph Depth
depth_computational_graph.summary: The length of the longest path through a flowchart describing how to compute outputs given inputs (p. 7).

depth_probabilistic_graph.label: Probabilistic Modeling Depth
depth_probabilistic_graph.summary: The depth of the graph describing how concepts are related to each other, regardless of the computational steps to compute them (p. 7).

linear_algebra.label: Linear Algebra
linear_algebra.summary: The branch of mathematics dealing with vectors, matrices, and tensors, essential for deep learning (p. 31).

la_objects.label: Mathematical Objects
la_objects.summary: The fundamental building blocks of linear algebra.

scalar_def.label: Scalar
scalar_def.summary: A single number, typically written in italics with lower-case variable names (p. 31).

vector_def.label: Vector
vector_def.summary: An ordered array of numbers, where elements are identified by an index (p. 31).

matrix_def.label: Matrix
matrix_def.summary: A 2-D array of numbers where each element is identified by two indices (p. 32).

tensor_def.label: Tensor
tensor_def.summary: An array of numbers arranged on a regular grid with a variable number of axes (p. 33).

la_operations.label: Linear Algebra Operations
la_operations.summary: Standard manipulations applied to arrays of numbers.

transpose_def.label: Transpose
transpose_def.summary: The mirror image of a matrix across the main diagonal, defined as (A^T)_{i,j} = A_{j,i} (p. 33).

broadcasting_def.label: Broadcasting
broadcasting_def.summary: Implicitly copying a vector to multiple locations to allow the addition of a matrix and a vector (p. 33).

matrix_multiplication.label: Matrix Multiplication
matrix_multiplication.summary: The product of A (m x n) and B (n x p) resulting in C (m x p), where C_{i,j} is the dot product of row i of A and column j of B (p. 34).

hadamard_product.label: Hadamard Product
hadamard_product.summary: The element-wise product of two matrices of the same shape (p. 34).

la_vector_spaces.label: Vector Spaces and Dependence
la_vector_spaces.summary: Concepts regarding the reach and redundancy of vectors.

linear_combination_def.label: Linear Combination
linear_combination_def.summary: The result of multiplying vectors by scalar coefficients and adding the results (p. 37).

span_def.label: Span
span_def.summary: The set of all points obtainable by linear combination of a set of vectors (p. 37).

column_space_def.label: Column Space (Range)
column_space_def.summary: The span of the columns of a matrix (p. 37).

linear_dependence_def.label: Linear Dependence
linear_dependence_def.summary: A state where at least one vector in a set is a linear combination of the others (p. 38).

singular_matrix_def.label: Singular Matrix
singular_matrix_def.summary: A square matrix with linearly dependent columns, which cannot be inverted (p. 38).

la_norms.label: Norms
la_norms.summary: Functions that measure the size or length of a vector (p. 39).

lp_norm_def.label: Lp Norm
lp_norm_def.summary: Defined as the p-th root of the sum of absolute values of elements raised to the p-th power (p. 39).

l2_norm_def.label: L2 Norm (Euclidean)
l2_norm_def.summary: The Euclidean distance from the origin to the point identified by the vector (p. 39).

l1_norm_def.label: L1 Norm
l1_norm_def.summary: The sum of the absolute values of the vector's elements; used when discriminating between zero and non-zero is critical (p. 39).

linf_norm_def.label: L-infinity Norm (Max Norm)
linf_norm_def.summary: The absolute value of the element with the largest magnitude in the vector (p. 40).

frobenius_norm_def.label: Frobenius Norm
frobenius_norm_def.summary: The L2 norm applied to the elements of a matrix (p. 40).

diagonal_matrix_def.label: Diagonal Matrix
diagonal_matrix_def.summary: A matrix where all entries outside the main diagonal are zero (p. 40).

symmetric_matrix_def.label: Symmetric Matrix
symmetric_matrix_def.summary: A matrix that is equal to its own transpose (A = A^T) (p. 40).

orthogonal_matrix_def.label: Orthogonal Matrix
orthogonal_matrix_def.summary: A square matrix whose rows and columns are mutually orthonormal, implying A^T A = A A^T = I and A^-1 = A^T (p. 41).

unit_vector_def.label: Unit Vector
unit_vector_def.summary: A vector with a norm of 1 (p. 40).

la_decompositions.label: Matrix Decompositions
la_decompositions.summary: Breaking matrices into constituent parts to reveal functional properties.

eigendecomposition_concept.label: Eigendecomposition
eigendecomposition_concept.summary: Decomposing a square matrix into eigenvectors (v) and eigenvalues (lambda) such that Av = lambda*v (p. 42).

positive_definite_def.label: Definiteness
positive_definite_def.summary: Matrices are positive definite if all eigenvalues are positive; positive semidefinite if all are positive or zero (p. 43).

svd_concept.label: Singular Value Decomposition (SVD)
svd_concept.summary: Factorizing any real matrix A into U D V^T, where U and V are orthogonal and D is diagonal (p. 44).

identity_matrix_def.label: Identity Matrix
identity_matrix_def.summary: A square matrix with 1s on the main diagonal and 0s elsewhere; preserves any vector it multiplies (p. 36).

matrix_inverse_def.label: Matrix Inverse
matrix_inverse_def.summary: A matrix A^-1 such that A^-1 A = I (p. 36).

pseudoinverse_def.label: Moore-Penrose Pseudoinverse
pseudoinverse_def.summary: A generalization of the inverse for non-square or singular matrices, providing the minimal L2 norm solution (p. 45).

trace_operator_def.label: Trace Operator
trace_operator_def.summary: The sum of the diagonal entries of a matrix; invariant to cyclic permutations (p. 46).

determinant_def.label: Determinant
determinant_def.summary: A scalar equal to the product of all eigenvalues; measures how multiplication by the matrix expands or contracts space (p. 47).

pca_example.label: Principal Components Analysis (PCA)
pca_example.summary: A lossy compression algorithm that finds the orthogonal basis (principal components) that minimizes the L2 distance between inputs and reconstructions (p. 47).

pca_fact_1.label: PCA Implementation
pca_fact_1.summary: The optimal basis is given by the eigenvectors of X^T X corresponding to the largest eigenvalues (p. 51).

probability_information_theory.label: Probability and Information Theory
probability_information_theory.summary: A framework for representing and quantifying uncertainty (p. 53).

prob_foundations.label: Probability Foundations
prob_foundations.summary: The conceptual motivations for using probability in AI.

uncertainty_sources.label: Sources of Uncertainty
uncertainty_sources.summary: Three primary origins: Inherent stochasticity, Incomplete observability, and Incomplete modeling (p. 54).

frequentist_vs_bayesian.label: Frequentist vs. Bayesian Probability
frequentist_vs_bayesian.summary: Frequentist probability refers to the rates at which events occur; Bayesian probability represents a degree of belief (p. 55).

random_variables.label: Random Variables
random_variables.summary: Variables that can take on different values randomly (p. 56).

discrete_rv.label: Discrete Random Variable
discrete_rv.summary: A variable with a finite or countably infinite number of states (p. 56).

continuous_rv.label: Continuous Random Variable
continuous_rv.summary: A variable associated with a real value (p. 56).

prob_distributions.label: Probability Distributions
prob_distributions.summary: Descriptions of how likely a random variable is to take on each possible state.

pmf_def.label: Probability Mass Function (PMF)
pmf_def.summary: Used for discrete variables; maps states to probabilities. Must be normalized to sum to 1 (p. 57).

pdf_def.label: Probability Density Function (PDF)
pdf_def.summary: Used for continuous variables; the probability of a state is the integral of the PDF over a region. Must integrate to 1 (p. 57).

marginal_prob_def.label: Marginal Probability
marginal_prob_def.summary: The probability distribution over a subset of variables, calculated by summing (discrete) or integrating (continuous) over the other variables (p. 58).

conditional_prob_def.label: Conditional Probability
conditional_prob_def.summary: The probability of an event given that another event has occurred: P(y|x) = P(x,y) / P(x) (p. 58).

prob_laws.label: Probability Laws
prob_laws.summary: Formal rules for deriving new uncertain statements.

chain_rule_prob.label: Chain Rule of Conditional Probabilities
chain_rule_prob.summary: A joint distribution can be decomposed into a product of conditional distributions (p. 59).

independence_def.label: Independence
independence_def.summary: Two variables are independent if their joint distribution is the product of their marginals (p. 60).

prob_stats.label: Probabilistic Statistics
prob_stats.summary: Measures of central tendency and dispersion.

expectation_def.label: Expectation (Expected Value)
expectation_def.summary: The average or mean value a function takes on when its argument is drawn from a distribution (p. 60).

variance_def.label: Variance
variance_def.summary: A measure of how much values of a function vary as samples are drawn from a distribution (p. 60).

covariance_def.label: Covariance
covariance_def.summary: A measure of how two variables are linearly related; zero covariance does not necessarily imply independence (p. 61).

common_distributions.label: Common Probability Distributions
common_distributions.summary: Standard distributions used in machine learning (p. 62).

bernoulli_dist.label: Bernoulli Distribution
bernoulli_dist.summary: Distribution over a single binary random variable, parameterized by phi (probability of being 1) (p. 62).

multinoulli_dist.label: Multinoulli (Categorical) Distribution
multinoulli_dist.summary: Distribution over a discrete variable with k finite states (p. 62).

gaussian_dist.label: Gaussian (Normal) Distribution
gaussian_dist.summary: A bell-shaped distribution over real numbers, parameterized by mean (mu) and variance (sigma^2) (p. 63).

multivariate_normal_dist.label: Multivariate Normal Distribution
multivariate_normal_dist.summary: Generalization of the Gaussian distribution to R^n, parameterized by a mean vector (mu) and a covariance matrix (Sigma) (p. 64).

numerical_computation.label: Numerical Computation
numerical_computation.summary: Computational challenges and optimization techniques (TOC p. 80).

ml_basics.label: Machine Learning Basics
ml_basics.summary: Foundational goals and algorithms of machine learning (TOC p. 98).

deep_networks.label: Deep Networks: Modern Practices
deep_networks.summary: established deep learning algorithms and practical methodologies (TOC p. 166).

dl_research.label: Deep Learning Research
dl_research.summary: Speculative ideas and advanced theoretical frameworks in deep learning (TOC p. 486).

prob_dist.label: Probability Distributions
prob_dist.summary: Various probability distributions used to model data, ranging from simple parametric forms to complex mixtures.

sharp_peak_dist.label: Sharp Peak Distributions
sharp_peak_dist.summary: Distributions used to place a sharp point of probability mass at specific values.

exp_dist.label: Exponential Distribution
exp_dist.summary: A distribution with a sharp point at x=0, assigning probability zero to all negative values using an indicator function. (p. 65)

laplace_dist.label: Laplace Distribution
laplace_dist.summary: A distribution allowing a sharp peak of probability mass at an arbitrary point mu. (p. 65)

delta_empirical.label: Dirac and Empirical Distributions
delta_empirical.summary: Distributions that cluster mass around single points or sets of samples.

dirac_delta.label: Dirac Delta Function
dirac_delta.summary: A generalized function that is zero-valued everywhere except 0, yet integrates to 1; used to create an infinitely narrow and high peak of mass. (p. 65)

empirical_dist.label: Empirical Distribution
empirical_dist.summary: A distribution that puts probability mass 1/m on each of m points in a dataset. For continuous variables, it is a mixture of Dirac components; for discrete variables, it is a multinoulli distribution based on empirical frequency. (p. 66)

mixture_models.label: Mixtures of Distributions
mixture_models.summary: Complex distributions created by combining simpler component distributions.

mixture_def.label: Mixture Distribution Definition
mixture_def.summary: A distribution where a component identity is first sampled from a multinoulli distribution, and then a sample is drawn from the chosen component. (p. 66)

latent_vars.label: Latent Variables
latent_vars.summary: Random variables that cannot be observed directly, such as the component identity variable c in a mixture model. (p. 67)

gmm.label: Gaussian Mixture Model (GMM)
gmm.summary: A powerful mixture model where components are Gaussians with separate means and covariances. It acts as a universal approximator of densities. (p. 67)

math_funcs.label: Useful Mathematical Functions
math_funcs.summary: Common functions used to parameterize probability distributions in deep learning.

logistic_sigmoid.label: Logistic Sigmoid
logistic_sigmoid.summary: A function with range (0,1), used to produce Bernoulli parameters. It saturates for very positive or negative arguments. (p. 67)

softplus.label: Softplus Function
softplus.summary: A smoothed version of the positive part function max(0, x), with range (0, infinity), useful for producing normal distribution parameters beta or sigma. (p. 68)

prob_theory.label: Probability Theory Essentials
prob_theory.summary: Fundamental rules and technical considerations for continuous random variables.

bayes_rule.label: Bayes' Rule
bayes_rule.summary: A formula to compute P(x|y) using P(y|x), P(x), and P(y). (p. 70)

continuous_vars_tech.label: Technical Details of Continuous Variables
continuous_vars_tech.summary: Advanced mathematical concepts required for a formal understanding of PDFs.

measure_theory.label: Measure Theory
measure_theory.summary: A branch of mathematics used to resolve paradoxes in set integration and define sets of 'measure zero' (negligibly small) and properties that hold 'almost everywhere'. (p. 71)

jacobian_transform.label: Change of Variables (Jacobian)
jacobian_transform.summary: When transforming a random variable y = g(x), the PDF py(y) is not simply px(g^-1(y)) but must account for the distortion of space via the determinant of the Jacobian matrix. (p. 72)

info_theory.label: Information Theory
info_theory.summary: The quantification of information present in signals and the similarity between distributions.

self_info.label: Self-Information
self_info.summary: The information gained by observing an event x, defined as I(x) = -log P(x). Measured in nats (base e) or bits (base 2). (p. 73)

shannon_entropy.label: Shannon Entropy
shannon_entropy.summary: The expected amount of information in an event drawn from a distribution; a measure of uncertainty. (p. 73)

kl_divergence.label: Kullback-Leibler (KL) Divergence
kl_divergence.summary: A non-negative, asymmetric measure of the difference between two distributions P and Q. (p. 74)

cross_entropy.label: Cross-Entropy
cross_entropy.summary: A measure related to KL divergence: H(P, Q) = H(P) + DKL(P||Q). Minimizing cross-entropy with respect to Q is equivalent to minimizing KL divergence. (p. 75)

graph_models.label: Structured Probabilistic Models
graph_models.summary: Representations of probability distributions using graphs to define factorizations.

directed_models.label: Directed Graphical Models
directed_models.summary: Models using directed edges to represent factorizations into conditional probability distributions. (p. 77)

undirected_models.label: Undirected Graphical Models
undirected_models.summary: Models using undirected edges to represent factorizations into non-negative functions (factors) over cliques, normalized by a constant Z. (p. 78)

num_comp.label: Numerical Computation
num_comp.summary: Practical issues when implementing mathematical functions on digital computers.

numerical_stability.label: Numerical Stability
numerical_stability.summary: Issues related to the finite representation of real numbers.

overflow_underflow.label: Overflow and Underflow
overflow_underflow.summary: Underflow occurs when numbers near zero are rounded to zero; overflow occurs when large magnitude numbers are approximated as infinity. (p. 80)

softmax_stabilization.label: Softmax Stabilization
softmax_stabilization.summary: Softmax is stabilized against overflow/underflow by subtracting the maximum input value (maxi xi) from the input vector. (p. 81)

poor_conditioning.label: Poor Conditioning
poor_conditioning.summary: Refers to functions that change rapidly with small input changes. For matrices, the condition number is the ratio of the largest to smallest eigenvalue. (p. 82)

opt_theory.label: Optimization Theory
opt_theory.summary: The process of minimizing or maximizing an objective (cost/loss) function.

gradient_based_opt.label: Gradient-Based Optimization
gradient_based_opt.summary: Optimization using the first and second derivatives of a function.

gradient_descent.label: Gradient Descent
gradient_descent.summary: An iterative algorithm that moves in the direction of the negative gradient to find a minimum. (p. 83)

critical_points.label: Critical Points
critical_points.summary: Points where the gradient is zero. Types include local minima, local maxima, and saddle points. (p. 83)

hessian_jacobian.label: Jacobian and Hessian Matrices
hessian_jacobian.summary: The Jacobian contains all first-order partial derivatives for vector-valued functions; the Hessian contains all second-order partial derivatives for scalar-valued functions and describes curvature. (p. 85-86)

newton_method.label: Newton's Method
newton_method.summary: A second-order optimization algorithm that uses the Hessian to jump directly toward the critical point of a quadratic approximation. (p. 91)

constrained_opt.label: Constrained Optimization
constrained_opt.summary: Finding the extremum of a function within a feasible set S.

lagrangian.label: Generalized Lagrangian
lagrangian.summary: A function combining the objective function and constraints using multipliers (lambda for equality, alpha for inequality). (p. 94)

kkt_approach.label: Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) Conditions
kkt_approach.summary: Necessary conditions for optimality: zero gradient of Lagrangian, satisfied constraints, and complementary slackness (alpha * h = 0). (p. 95)

learning_framework.label: Learning Algorithm Framework
learning_framework.summary: A system that improves performance P at tasks T using experience E. (p. 98)

ml_tasks.label: Machine Learning Tasks
ml_tasks.summary: Common tasks including Classification, Regression, Transcription, Translation, Structured Output, Anomaly Detection, Synthesis/Sampling, Imputation, Denoising, and Density Estimation. (p. 99-102)

performance_measures.label: Performance Measures
performance_measures.summary: Quantitative measures like accuracy (0-1 loss) for classification or average log-probability for density estimation. (p. 103)

learning_paradigms.label: Learning Paradigms
learning_paradigms.summary: Categorization of learning based on the type of experience E.

unsupervised_learning.label: Unsupervised Learning
unsupervised_learning.summary: Learning the structure of data (e.g., p(x)) without labels; includes clustering and density estimation. (p. 104)

supervised_learning.label: Supervised Learning
supervised_learning.summary: Learning to predict a target y given features x (e.g., estimating p(y|x)) using labeled data. (p. 104)

generalization_theory.label: Generalization Theory
generalization_theory.summary: The ability of a model to perform well on previously unobserved inputs.

capacity_concepts.label: Model Capacity
capacity_concepts.summary: The ability of a model to fit a wide variety of functions. Representational capacity is the family of functions available; effective capacity is limited by optimization. (p. 111)

overunderfitting.label: Overfitting and Underfitting
overunderfitting.summary: Underfitting: unable to achieve low training error. Overfitting: large gap between training error and generalization error. (p. 111)

regularization.label: Regularization
regularization.summary: Any modification intended to reduce generalization error but not training error, such as weight decay (penalizing L2 norm of weights). (p. 118)

no_free_lunch.label: No Free Lunch Theorem
no_free_lunch.summary: States that averaged over all possible data distributions, every classification algorithm has the same error rate on unobserved points. (p. 116)

evaluation_metrics.label: Evaluation and Hyperparameters
evaluation_metrics.summary: Methods for tuning and assessing model performance.

hyperparameters.label: Hyperparameters
hyperparameters.summary: Settings that control the learning algorithm and are not adapted by the algorithm itself (e.g., polynomial degree, lambda for weight decay). (p. 120)

validation_sets.label: Validation Sets
validation_sets.summary: A subset of training data used to tune hyperparameters to avoid overfitting the training set. (p. 121)

cross_validation.label: K-Fold Cross-Validation
cross_validation.summary: A procedure to estimate generalization error by splitting data into k folds and averaging error across k trials. (p. 122)

statistical_estimation.label: Statistical Estimation
statistical_estimation.summary: Formal methods for parameter and function estimation.

point_estimation.label: Point Estimation
point_estimation.summary: Providing a single best prediction for a parameter theta or a function f. (p. 122)

bias_variance.label: Bias-Variance Trade-off
bias_variance.summary: Bias measures expected deviation from true value; Variance measures deviation caused by sampling. MSE = Bias^2 + Variance. (p. 124, 129)

consistency.label: Consistency
consistency.summary: A property where the point estimate converges in probability to the true value as the number of samples m goes to infinity. (p. 130)

mle.label: Maximum Likelihood Estimation (MLE)
mle.summary: Finding parameters theta that maximize the probability of the observed data; equivalent to minimizing the KL divergence between the empirical and model distributions. (p. 131)

maximum_likelihood.label: Maximum Likelihood Estimation (MLE)
maximum_likelihood.summary: A method of estimating parameters by maximizing the likelihood of the observed data.

mle_consistency.label: MLE Consistency
mle_consistency.summary: The property that as the number of training examples m approaches infinity, the estimate converges to the true parameter value.

consistency_cond_1.label: Model Family Condition
consistency_cond_1.summary: The true distribution p_data must lie within the model family p_model(theta); otherwise, no estimator can recover p_data. (Page 134)

consistency_cond_2.label: Identifiability Condition
consistency_cond_2.summary: The true distribution p_data must correspond to exactly one value of theta to determine which value was used by the data generating process. (Page 134)

statistical_efficiency.label: Statistical Efficiency
statistical_efficiency.summary: The ability of a consistent estimator to obtain lower generalization error for a fixed number of samples m.

cramer_rao_bound.label: Cramér-Rao Lower Bound
cramer_rao_bound.summary: For large m, the Cramér-Rao lower bound shows that no consistent estimator has a lower mean squared error than the MLE. (Page 134)

mle_overfitting.label: MLE and Overfitting
mle_overfitting.summary: When training data is limited, regularization strategies like weight decay can be used to obtain a biased version of MLE with less variance. (Page 134)

bayesian_statistics.label: Bayesian Statistics
bayesian_statistics.summary: A statistical perspective where parameters theta are treated as random variables reflecting degrees of certainty.

bayesian_components.label: Bayesian Components
bayesian_components.summary: The elements used to update beliefs about parameters.

prior_distribution.label: Prior Distribution p(theta)
prior_distribution.summary: Represents knowledge of theta before observing data; often chosen as broad (high entropy) or reflecting a preference for simpler solutions. (Page 135)

likelihood.label: Data Likelihood p(x|theta)
likelihood.summary: The probability of observing the data given a specific parameter value theta. (Page 135)

posterior_distribution.label: Posterior Distribution p(theta|x)
posterior_distribution.summary: The updated belief about theta after observing data, calculated via Bayes' rule: p(theta|x) proportional to p(x|theta)p(theta). (Page 135)

bayesian_prediction.label: Bayesian Prediction
bayesian_prediction.summary: Predictions are made by integrating over the full posterior distribution of theta rather than using a point estimate. (Page 136)

map_estimation.label: Maximum A Posteriori (MAP)
map_estimation.summary: A point estimate that chooses the value of theta with the maximal posterior probability. (Page 138)

map_formula.label: MAP Objective Function
map_formula.summary: theta_MAP = arg max [ log p(x|theta) + log p(theta) ], combining the log-likelihood and log-prior. (Page 139)

map_vs_mle.label: MAP vs MLE
map_vs_mle.summary: MAP leverages prior information to reduce variance compared to MLE, but introduces bias. Weight decay in ML is equivalent to MAP with a Gaussian prior. (Page 139)

probabilistic_supervised.label: Probabilistic Supervised Learning
probabilistic_supervised.summary: Learning by estimating a conditional probability distribution p(y|x, theta).

linear_regression_prob.label: Probabilistic Linear Regression
linear_regression_prob.summary: Assumes a Gaussian conditional distribution p(y|x, theta) = N(theta^T x, I). (Page 140)

logistic_regression.label: Logistic Regression
logistic_regression.summary: Used for binary classification by squashing a linear function into (0, 1) using the logistic sigmoid function: p(y=1|x, theta) = sigma(theta^T x). (Page 140)

svm.label: Support Vector Machines (SVM)
svm.summary: A non-probabilistic model that outputs class identity based on the sign of w^T x + b. (Page 141)

kernel_trick.label: The Kernel Trick
kernel_trick.summary: Replacing dot products between examples with a kernel function k(x, x') = phi(x)^T phi(x'), allowing learning in high-dimensional feature spaces without explicit mapping. (Page 141)

gaussian_rbf_kernel.label: Gaussian/RBF Kernel
gaussian_rbf_kernel.summary: A common kernel that acts as a template match; value decreases as Euclidean distance between u and v increases. (Page 142)

support_vectors.label: Support Vectors
support_vectors.summary: Training examples with non-zero alpha coefficients that define the decision boundary in an SVM. (Page 142)

knn.label: k-Nearest Neighbors (k-NN)
knn.summary: A non-parametric algorithm that predicts output y by averaging the values of the k-nearest neighbors in the training set. (Page 143)

decision_trees.label: Decision Trees
decision_trees.summary: Divide the input space into non-overlapping regions using axis-aligned cuts, mapping each leaf node region to a constant output. (Page 145)

low_dim_rep.label: Low-Dimensional Representations
low_dim_rep.summary: Compressing information into a smaller representation by removing redundancies. (Page 147)

sparse_rep.label: Sparse Representations
sparse_rep.summary: Embedding data into a representation where most entries are zero for any given input. (Page 147)

independent_rep.label: Independent Representations
independent_rep.summary: Disentangling sources of variation so that dimensions are statistically independent. (Page 147)

pca.label: Principal Components Analysis (PCA)
pca.summary: A linear orthogonal transformation that projects data to a lower-dimensional space, aligning the direction of greatest variance with the new axes. (Page 148)

pca_uncorrelated.label: PCA Decorrelation
pca_uncorrelated.summary: PCA ensures the covariance matrix of the transformed representation z is diagonal, meaning elements are mutually uncorrelated. (Page 149)

pca_svd.label: PCA via SVD
pca_svd.summary: Principal components are the right singular vectors W of the design matrix X in the decomposition X = U W Sigma^T. (Page 149)

kmeans.label: k-means Clustering
kmeans.summary: Algorithm that partitions data into k clusters by alternating between assigning examples to the nearest centroid and updating centroids to the mean of assigned examples. (Page 150)

optimization_sgd.label: Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD)
optimization_sgd.summary: An extension of gradient descent that approximates the gradient using a small minibatch of examples.

sgd_minibatch.label: Minibatch Gradient Estimation
sgd_minibatch.summary: Gradient is estimated as g = (1/m') sum_{i=1 to m'} grad L(x_i, y_i, theta), where m' is a small fixed size. (Page 152)

sgd_cost_complexity.label: SGD Computational Cost
sgd_cost_complexity.summary: The cost per update is O(1) with respect to training set size m, making it scalable to billions of examples. (Page 152)

dl_motivations.label: Motivations for Deep Learning
dl_motivations.summary: Challenges in high-dimensional data that traditional ML algorithms fail to address.

curse_of_dimensionality.label: Curse of Dimensionality
curse_of_dimensionality.summary: The phenomenon where the number of distinct configurations of variables increases exponentially O(v^d) as dimensions d increase, making data sparse. (Page 155)

smoothness_prior.label: Smoothness/Local Constancy Prior
smoothness_prior.summary: The belief that f(x) should be approximately equal to f(x + epsilon). Traditional algorithms rely on this, but it fails in high dimensions because most grid cells are empty. (Page 157)

manifold_hypothesis.label: Manifold Hypothesis
manifold_hypothesis.summary: The assumption that high-dimensional data is actually concentrated near a low-dimensional connected region (manifold) embedded in the higher-dimensional space. (Page 161)

deep_feedforward_networks.label: Deep Feedforward Networks (MLPs)
deep_feedforward_networks.summary: Function approximators consisting of an input layer, one or more hidden layers, and an output layer, where information flows in one direction.

dfn_architecture.label: DFN Architecture
dfn_architecture.summary: The structure of the network, defined by depth (number of layers) and width (units per layer).

hidden_layers_purpose.label: Role of Hidden Layers
hidden_layers_purpose.summary: Hidden layers are used to learn a representation phi(x) that transforms the input into a space where the target function is easier to approximate (e.g., linearly). (Page 169)

learning_phi.label: Learning the Transformation phi
learning_phi.summary: Unlike manual feature engineering, deep learning uses optimization to find the parameters theta that define the best transformation phi(x; theta). (Page 170)

dfn_activation_functions.label: Activation Functions
dfn_activation_functions.summary: Nonlinear functions applied element-wise to the output of an affine transformation to enable the network to represent nonlinear functions.

relu_units.label: Rectified Linear Units (ReLU)
relu_units.summary: g(z) = max(0, z). Default recommendation; preserves gradients for active units and is computationally efficient. (Page 174)

leaky_prelu.label: Leaky ReLU and PReLU
leaky_prelu.summary: Generalizations of ReLU that use a non-zero slope alpha for z < 0 to ensure gradients are received everywhere. (Page 193)

maxout_units.label: Maxout Units
maxout_units.summary: Divide inputs into groups and output the maximum element of each group; can approximate any convex function. (Page 193)

sigmoidal_units.label: Sigmoidal Units
sigmoidal_units.summary: Logistic sigmoid and tanh. Now discouraged for hidden layers due to saturation, which causes vanishing gradients. (Page 195)

dfn_output_units.label: Output Units
dfn_output_units.summary: The final layer transformation that adapts hidden features to the specific task.

linear_output.label: Linear Output Units
linear_output.summary: y_hat = W^T h + b. Used for Gaussian output distributions; MLE corresponds to MSE. (Page 181)

sigmoid_output.label: Sigmoid Output Units
sigmoid_output.summary: y_hat = sigma(W^T h + b). Used for Bernoulli distributions (binary classification). (Page 182)

softmax_output.label: Softmax Output Units
softmax_output.summary: Generalization of sigmoid for Multinoulli distributions (n-classes); outputs sum to 1. (Page 184)

mixture_density_output.label: Mixture Density Networks (MDN)
mixture_density_output.summary: Output a Gaussian mixture distribution to handle multimodal regression, predicting mixture components, means, and covariances. (Page 189)

dfn_approximation_theory.label: Approximation Theory
dfn_approximation_theory.summary: Mathematical foundations regarding the capacity of feedforward networks.

universal_approximation_theorem.label: Universal Approximation Theorem
universal_approximation_theorem.summary: A network with one hidden layer and a squashing activation function can approximate any Borel measurable function, provided it has enough units. (Page 198)

depth_advantage.label: The Advantage of Depth
depth_advantage.summary: Deep networks can represent functions with a number of linear regions that grows exponentially with depth l, whereas shallow networks may require an exponential number of units to achieve the same capacity. (Page 199)

nn_architecture.label: Neural Network Architecture
nn_architecture.summary: The structural design of neural networks, focusing on depth, connectivity, and specialized task-based architectures.

deep_models.label: Deep Models
deep_models.summary: Models characterized by multiple layers of function composition.

compositional_belief.label: Compositional Belief
compositional_belief.summary: The prior belief that the target function consists of a composition of several simpler functions.

representation_learning_view.label: Representation Learning View
representation_learning_view.summary: The belief that learning involves discovering underlying factors of variation described by simpler underlying factors.

program_view.label: Computer Program View
program_view.summary: The belief that the function is a program with multiple sequential steps where each step uses the previous output (e.g., counters or pointers).

depth_generalization_fact.label: Depth and Generalization
depth_generalization_fact.summary: Empirical evidence suggests greater depth results in better generalization across various tasks (Bengio et al. 2007, Erhan et al. 2009).

architectural_diversity.label: Architectural Diversity
architectural_diversity.summary: Variations in network structure beyond simple chains of layers.

cnn_concept.label: Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs)
cnn_concept.summary: Specialized architectures for computer vision using sparse connection patterns.

connectivity_strategies.label: Connectivity Strategies
connectivity_strategies.summary: Methods for connecting layers to optimize gradient flow and computation.

skip_connections.label: Skip Connections
skip_connections.summary: Connections from layer i to layer i+2 or higher, facilitating gradient flow from output to input layers.

sparse_connectivity.label: Sparse Connectivity
sparse_connectivity.summary: Reducing connections so input units connect only to a subset of output units, reducing parameters and computation.

backpropagation.label: Back-Propagation
backpropagation.summary: The algorithmic method for computing gradients of a cost function with respect to model parameters.

propagation_phases.label: Propagation Phases
propagation_phases.summary: The two-step process of information flow in a neural network.

forward_prop.label: Forward Propagation
forward_prop.summary: Information flows from input x through hidden units to produce output y-hat and scalar cost J(theta).

backward_prop.label: Backward Propagation
backward_prop.summary: Information flows backwards from the cost to compute the gradient of the function.

computational_graphs.label: Computational Graphs
computational_graphs.summary: A formal language where nodes represent variables (scalars, vectors, tensors) and edges represent operations.

graph_variable_node.label: Variable Node
graph_variable_node.summary: A node in the graph representing a tensor of arbitrary dimensionality.

graph_operation.label: Operation
graph_operation.summary: A simple function of one or more variables returning a single output variable.

chain_rule_calculus.label: Chain Rule of Calculus
chain_rule_calculus.summary: The mathematical foundation used to compute derivatives of composed functions.

scalar_chain_rule.label: Scalar Chain Rule
scalar_chain_rule.summary: For z = f(g(x)), dz/dx = dz/dy * dy/dx, where y = g(x).

vector_tensor_chain_rule.label: Vector/Tensor Chain Rule
vector_tensor_chain_rule.summary: The gradient is obtained by multiplying a Jacobian matrix by a gradient vector. For tensors, this is handled as Jacobian-gradient products.

backprop_implementation.label: Backprop Implementation
backprop_implementation.summary: The practical execution of the chain rule to compute gradients efficiently.

dynamic_programming_backprop.label: Dynamic Programming in Backprop
dynamic_programming_backprop.summary: Backprop avoids exponential explosion of repeated subexpressions by storing intermediate results in a table (Dynamic Programming).

symbol_to_number.label: Symbol-to-Number Differentiation
symbol_to_number.summary: Returns numerical values for the gradient at specific input values (e.g., Torch, Caffe).

symbol_to_symbol.label: Symbol-to-Symbol Differentiation
symbol_to_symbol.summary: Constructs a symbolic graph of the derivatives, allowing for higher-order derivatives (e.g., Theano, TensorFlow).

general_backprop_skeleton.label: General Backprop Skeleton
general_backprop_skeleton.summary: Uses a graph G where each operation 'op' has a 'bprop' method that computes a Jacobian-vector product for its inputs.

bias_variance_tradeoff.label: Bias-Variance Tradeoff
bias_variance_tradeoff.summary: Regularization works by trading increased bias for reduced variance to move a model from an overfit regime to a matched regime.

parameter_norm_penalties.label: Parameter Norm Penalties
parameter_norm_penalties.summary: Limiting model capacity by adding a penalty term Omega(theta) to the objective function J.

l2_regularization.label: L2 Regularization (Weight Decay)
l2_regularization.summary: Adds a penalty proportional to the squared L2 norm of weights. Shrinks weights towards the origin; rescales optimal weights along Hessian eigenvectors.

l2_bayesian_prior.label: L2 Bayesian Prior
l2_bayesian_prior.summary: Equivalent to MAP Bayesian inference with a Gaussian prior on the weights.

l2_linear_regression_effect.label: L2 Linear Regression Effect
l2_linear_regression_effect.summary: Replaces the covariance matrix X^T*X with (X^T*X + alpha*I), making it invertible and shrinking weights of low-covariance features.

l1_regularization.label: L1 Regularization
l1_regularization.summary: Adds a penalty proportional to the sum of absolute values of weights. Induces sparsity (weights become exactly zero), acting as feature selection (LASSO).

l1_bayesian_prior.label: L1 Bayesian Prior
l1_bayesian_prior.summary: Equivalent to MAP Bayesian inference with an isotropic Laplace distribution over weights.

constrained_optimization.label: Constrained Optimization
constrained_optimization.summary: Imposing explicit constraints Omega(theta) < k instead of penalties.

lagrange_multipliers.label: Lagrange Multipliers
lagrange_multipliers.summary: Using KKT multipliers to solve constrained problems by creating a generalized Lagrange function.

explicit_reprojection.label: Explicit Reprojection
explicit_reprojection.summary: Taking a gradient step and then projecting theta back to the constraint region. Prevents 'dead units' and numerical overflow.

dataset_augmentation.label: Dataset Augmentation
dataset_augmentation.summary: Creating synthetic training data through transformations (translation, rotation, scaling) to force model invariance.

noise_robustness.label: Noise Robustness
noise_robustness.summary: Adding noise to inputs, hidden units, or weights to improve generalization.

weight_noise_effect.label: Weight Noise Effect
weight_noise_effect.summary: Pushes the model into regions of parameter space where small perturbations have small influence (flat minima).

label_smoothing.label: Label Smoothing
label_smoothing.summary: Replacing hard targets (0, 1) with soft targets (epsilon, 1-epsilon) to prevent the softmax from pursuing unreachable probabilities.

semi_supervised_learning.label: Semi-Supervised Learning
semi_supervised_learning.summary: Combining labeled and unlabeled data to learn representations where examples of the same class have similar representations.

multi_task_learning.label: Multi-Task Learning
multi_task_learning.summary: Sharing generic parameters across multiple tasks while maintaining task-specific upper layers.

early_stopping.label: Early Stopping
early_stopping.summary: Terminating training when validation error begins to rise. Acts as a computationally efficient hyperparameter selection for training time.

early_stopping_l2_equivalence.label: Early Stopping L2 Equivalence
early_stopping_l2_equivalence.summary: Under quadratic approximation, early stopping is equivalent to L2 regularization, where training iterations tau are inversely proportional to alpha.

parameter_sharing.label: Parameter Sharing/Tying
parameter_sharing.summary: Forcing different model components to use the same parameters to reduce memory and incorporate domain knowledge.

cnn_parameter_sharing.label: CNN Parameter Sharing
cnn_parameter_sharing.summary: Sharing weights across different image locations to achieve translation invariance.

representational_sparsity.label: Representational Sparsity
representational_sparsity.summary: Encouraging a representation h to have many zero elements through L1 penalties on activations or hard constraints like OMP-k.

ensemble_methods.label: Ensemble Methods
ensemble_methods.summary: Combining multiple hypotheses to reduce generalization error through model averaging.

bagging_concept.label: Bagging (Bootstrap Aggregating)
bagging_concept.summary: Training several models on datasets constructed by sampling with replacement, then averaging their outputs.

dropout_concept.label: Dropout
dropout_concept.summary: Approximate bagging by randomly dropping units (multiplying by 0) during training. Trains an ensemble of exponentially many sub-networks.

weight_scaling_inference.label: Weight Scaling Inference Rule
weight_scaling_inference.summary: Approximating the geometric mean of the ensemble by multiplying weights by the inclusion probability at test time.

dropout_computational_cost.label: Dropout Computational Cost
dropout_computational_cost.summary: Training requires O(n) per example; inference cost is identical to a standard network after a one-time weight scaling.

dropout.label: Dropout
dropout.summary: A regularization technique that implements a form of bagging with parameter sharing by randomly modifying hidden units during training.

dropout_bagging.label: Dropout as Bagging
dropout_bagging.summary: Dropout trains a bagged ensemble of models formed by including or excluding units, or by other random modifications.
dropout_bagging.details: Any random modification parametrized by vector µ is admissible. Multiplying weights by µ ~ N(1, I) can outperform binary masks because E[µ] = 1 allows the standard network to implement approximate inference without weight scaling. (p. 266)

dropout_biological_analogy.label: Biological Analogy: Sexual Reproduction
dropout_biological_analogy.summary: The idea that swapping genes creates evolutionary pressure for genes to be robust across different organisms.
dropout_biological_analogy.details: Dropout forces hidden units to perform well regardless of which other units are present, making them robust features that are good in many contexts. (p. 266)

dropout_feature_destruction.label: Adaptive Information Destruction
dropout_feature_destruction.summary: Dropout destroys extracted features rather than raw input values.
dropout_feature_destruction.details: Applying masking noise to hidden units is an intelligent destruction of information content. For example, dropping a 'nose' detector forces the model to learn redundant features (e.g., a 'mouth' detector) to identify a face. (p. 266)

dropout_noise_type.label: Multiplicative Noise
dropout_noise_type.summary: Dropout utilizes multiplicative noise to avoid pathological solutions.
dropout_noise_type.details: If noise were additive, a ReLU unit could simply learn to be very large to make the noise insignificant. Multiplicative noise prevents this. (p. 267)

adversarial_training.label: Adversarial Training
adversarial_training.summary: Training models on intentionally perturbed examples to increase robustness and reduce generalization error.

adversarial_examples.label: Adversarial Examples
adversarial_examples.summary: Inputs x' near x that are imperceptible to humans but cause the model to make highly different predictions.
adversarial_examples.details: These are constructed using optimization to find a point x' where the model output differs significantly from the output at x. (p. 268)

linearity_cause.label: Excessive Linearity
linearity_cause.summary: The primary cause of adversarial examples is the highly linear nature of neural network building blocks.
linearity_cause.details: Linear functions can change rapidly if they have numerous inputs. Adversarial training encourages local constancy in the neighborhood of training data. (p. 268)

virtual_adversarial_training.label: Virtual Adversarial Examples (VAE)
virtual_adversarial_training.summary: A semi-supervised learning technique using adversarial examples generated without true labels.
virtual_adversarial_training.details: The model assigns a label ˆy to an unlabeled point x and seeks an adversarial example x' that changes the label. The model is then trained to assign the same label to both. (p. 269)

manifold_regularization.label: Manifold-based Regularization
manifold_regularization.summary: Techniques based on the Manifold Hypothesis: the assumption that high-dimensional data lies near a low-dimensional manifold.

tangent_distance.label: Tangent Distance
tangent_distance.summary: A non-parametric nearest-neighbor algorithm using distances between tangent planes to manifolds.
tangent_distance.details: Approximates the distance between manifolds M1 and M2 by calculating the distance between their tangent planes at points x1 and x2. (p. 270)

tangent_prop.label: Tangent Propagation
tangent_prop.summary: Training with a penalty to make the output locally invariant to known factors of variation.
tangent_prop.details: Adds a regularization penalty Ω(θ) = Σ || ∇f(x) v_i ||^2, where v_i are known manifold tangent vectors. It regularizes infinitesimal perturbations. (p. 270)

manifold_tangent_classifier.label: Manifold Tangent Classifier
manifold_tangent_classifier.summary: A method that uses autoencoders to learn tangent vectors without requiring them a priori.
manifold_tangent_classifier.details: Uses unsupervised learning (autoencoders) to estimate manifold structure, then uses these tangents for regularization as in tangent prop. (p. 271)

optimization_fundamentals.label: Optimization Fundamentals
optimization_fundamentals.summary: The core principles of finding parameters that minimize a cost function in machine learning.

learning_vs_optimization.label: Learning vs. Pure Optimization
learning_vs_optimization.summary: Machine learning optimizes a proxy cost function J(θ) to improve an often intractable performance measure P on a test set.
learning_vs_optimization.details: In pure optimization, minimizing J is the goal. In learning, minimizing J is a means to improve generalization. (p. 274)

empirical_risk_minimization.label: Empirical Risk Minimization (ERM)
empirical_risk_minimization.summary: Minimizing the expected loss on the training set (empirical distribution) as a proxy for the true distribution risk.
empirical_risk_minimization.details: ERM is prone to overfitting as high-capacity models can memorize the training set. (p. 275)

surrogate_loss.label: Surrogate Loss Functions
surrogate_loss.summary: Using an optimizable proxy for a non-differentiable loss function (e.g., 0-1 loss).
surrogate_loss.details: Negative log-likelihood is a common surrogate for 0-1 loss, allowing the model to estimate conditional probabilities. (p. 276)

batch_methods.label: Batch and Minibatch Algorithms
batch_methods.summary: Different strategies for computing the gradient based on the amount of data processed per update.

batch_gradient_descent.label: Batch Gradient Descent
batch_gradient_descent.summary: Processes the entire training set to compute a single gradient update.
batch_gradient_descent.details: Deterministic method; computation time per update grows linearly with the number of training examples. (p. 278)

stochastic_gradient_descent.label: Stochastic/Online Methods
stochastic_gradient_descent.summary: Processes a single example per update.
stochastic_gradient_descent.details: Online methods specifically refer to examples drawn from a continuous stream. (p. 278)

minibatch_sgd.label: Minibatch SGD
minibatch_sgd.summary: Processes a subset of training examples per update.
minibatch_sgd.details: Balances gradient accuracy and computation speed. Factors affecting batch size include GPU memory, hardware alignment (powers of 2), and regularization effects of small batches. (p. 278-279)

optimization_challenges.label: Optimization Challenges
optimization_challenges.summary: The non-convex nature of neural network cost functions leads to several training difficulties.

ill_conditioning.label: Ill-Conditioning
ill_conditioning.summary: Issues with the Hessian matrix H causing gradients to be poorly scaled.
ill_conditioning.details: Manifests when the gᵀHg term grows significantly, forcing the learning rate to shrink to compensate for high curvature, slowing learning. (p. 282)

local_minima.label: Local Minima and Identifiability
local_minima.summary: The presence of many local minima due to weight space symmetry.
local_minima.details: Non-identifiability occurs because swapping hidden units (weight space symmetry) or scaling weights in ReLU networks results in equivalent models. In large networks, most local minima have low cost. (p. 283-284)

saddle_points.label: Saddle Points
saddle_points.summary: Points where the gradient is zero, but the Hessian has both positive and negative eigenvalues.
saddle_points.details: In high dimensions, saddle points are exponentially more common than local minima. Newton's method can be attracted to them, while SGD typically escapes them. (p. 285)

cliffs_exploding_gradients.label: Cliﬀs and Exploding Gradients
cliffs_exploding_gradients.summary: Extremely steep regions in the cost function caused by multiplying large weights.
cliffs_exploding_gradients.details: Updates on a cliff can catapult parameters far from their current position. Mitigated by gradient clipping. (p. 288)

long_term_dependencies.label: Long-Term Dependencies
long_term_dependencies.summary: Vanishing and exploding gradients in deep computational graphs.
long_term_dependencies.details: Repeated multiplication by a matrix W results in gradients scaled by diag(λ)ᵗ. Eigenvalues λ ≠ 1 cause gradients to explode or vanish. (p. 289)

optimization_algorithms.label: Optimization Algorithms
optimization_algorithms.summary: Specific iterative procedures used to update model parameters.

sgd_basic.label: Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD)
sgd_basic.summary: The fundamental algorithm updating parameters in the direction of the estimated gradient.
sgd_basic.details: Update rule: θ ← θ - εₖ ĝ. Requires learning rate decay to ensure convergence because sampling noise does not vanish at the minimum. (p. 294)

momentum_methods.label: Momentum Methods
momentum_methods.summary: Algorithms that use a moving average of gradients to accelerate learning and smooth noisy gradients.

standard_momentum.label: Standard Momentum
standard_momentum.summary: Introduces a velocity variable v as an exponentially decaying average of negative gradients.
standard_momentum.details: Analogy: a hockey puck sliding down an icy surface with viscous drag. Helps traverse narrow valleys. (p. 296-299)

nesterov_momentum.label: Nesterov Momentum
nesterov_momentum.summary: A variant where the gradient is evaluated after the velocity is applied.
nesterov_momentum.details: Acts as a correction factor to standard momentum. In convex batch cases, improves convergence from O(1/k) to O(1/k²). (p. 300)

adaptive_learning_rates.label: Adaptive Learning Rate Algorithms
adaptive_learning_rates.summary: Algorithms that maintain separate learning rates for each parameter.

adagrad.label: AdaGrad
adagrad.summary: Scales learning rates inversely proportional to the square root of the sum of historical squared gradients.
adagrad.details: Effective for convex optimization, but in deep learning, accumulation of squared gradients can cause premature decay of the learning rate. (p. 307)

rmsprop.label: RMSProp
rmsprop.summary: Modifies AdaGrad by using an exponentially weighted moving average of squared gradients.
rmsprop.details: Designed for non-convex settings to discard extreme past history, allowing convergence in local convex bowls. (p. 307)

adam.label: Adam (Adaptive Moments)
adam.summary: Combines RMSProp and Momentum with bias correction.
adam.details: Estimates first-order (momentum) and second-order (uncentered variance) moments of the gradient with exponential weighting. (p. 308)

second_order_methods.label: Approximate Second-Order Methods
second_order_methods.summary: Algorithms that use the Hessian matrix or its approximation to inform updates.

newtons_method.label: Newton's Method
newtons_method.summary: Uses a second-order Taylor expansion to jump directly to the minimum of a quadratic function.
newtons_method.details: Update: θ* = θ0 - H⁻¹∇J. Computationally expensive (O(k³) for k parameters) and attracted to saddle points. (p. 311)

conjugate_gradients.label: Conjugate Gradients
conjugate_gradients.summary: Avoids Hessian inversion by iteratively descending conjugate directions.
conjugate_gradients.details: Two directions are conjugate if dᵀ H d' = 0. Prevents zig-zagging patterns found in steepest descent. (p. 313)

bfgs.label: BFGS / L-BFGS
bfgs.summary: Quasi-Newton methods that iteratively refine an approximation of the inverse Hessian.
bfgs.details: L-BFGS (Limited Memory) reduces memory costs from O(n²) to O(n) by not storing the full matrix M. (p. 316)

initialization_strategies.label: Parameter Initialization
initialization_strategies.summary: Strategies for choosing the starting point θ0 to ensure convergence and stability.

symmetry_breaking.label: Symmetry Breaking
symmetry_breaking.summary: The requirement that different units begin with different parameters.
symmetry_breaking.details: Prevents units from computing the same function and avoids losing signal/gradient in the null space. Accomplished via random initialization. (p. 301)

weight_scaling.label: Weight Scaling Heuristics
weight_scaling.summary: Rules for setting the variance of initial weights to preserve signal variance.

xavier_initialization.label: Glorot/Xavier Initialization
xavier_initialization.summary: Initializes weights to compromise between activation variance and gradient variance.
xavier_initialization.details: Weights sampled from U(-√(6/(m+n)), √(6/(m+n))) where m=inputs and n=outputs. (p. 303)

orthogonal_initialization.label: Orthogonal Initialization
orthogonal_initialization.summary: Initializing weights as random orthogonal matrices.
orthogonal_initialization.details: Ensures convergence time is independent of depth for linear networks. (p. 303)

sparse_initialization.label: Sparse Initialization
sparse_initialization.summary: Initializing each unit to have exactly k non-zero weights.
sparse_initialization.details: Keeps total input independent of m without shrinking individual weights. (p. 304)

bias_initialization.label: Bias Initialization
bias_initialization.summary: Strategies for setting initial bias values.

marginal_statistics_bias.label: Marginal Statistics Bias
marginal_statistics_bias.summary: Setting output biases to match the marginal distribution of the targets.
marginal_statistics_bias.details: For example, solving softmax(b) = c where c is the class distribution. (p. 305)

relu_saturation_bias.label: ReLU Saturation Bias
relu_saturation_bias.summary: Setting biases to a small positive value (e.g., 0.1) to avoid initial saturation.
relu_saturation_bias.details: Ensures units are active at initialization. (p. 305)

gate_bias.label: Gate Bias
gate_bias.summary: Initializing biases to ensure gates are open at the start of training.
gate_bias.details: Example: Setting the LSTM forget gate bias to 1. (p. 305)

meta_optimization.label: Optimization Strategies and Meta-Algorithms
meta_optimization.summary: Higher-level templates and architectural designs that simplify optimization.

batch_normalization.label: Batch Normalization
batch_normalization.summary: A method of adaptive reparametrization that standardizes activations across a minibatch.

bn_formula.label: BN Reparametrization
bn_formula.summary: Replacing H with (H - µ)/σ, where µ and σ are minibatch mean and standard deviation.
bn_formula.details: Back-propagates through the mean and variance calculations. Prevents updates from simply shifting the mean/variance. (p. 318)

bn_training_vs_test.label: BN Training vs. Test
bn_training_vs_test.summary: Uses minibatch statistics during training and running averages during testing.
bn_training_vs_test.details: Running averages allow evaluation on single examples. (p. 319)

bn_expressive_power.label: Maintaining Expressive Power
bn_expressive_power.summary: Introduces learned parameters γ and β to allow the network to undo normalization if necessary.
bn_expressive_power.details: The transformed output is γH' + β. This separates the mean/variance from the complex interactions of lower layers. (p. 320)

coordinate_descent.label: Coordinate Descent
coordinate_descent.summary: Optimizing a subset of variables while keeping others fixed.
coordinate_descent.details: Useful when variables can be separated into isolated groups, such as dictionary parameters W and code representations H in sparse coding. (p. 321)

polyak_averaging.label: Polyak Averaging
polyak_averaging.summary: Averaging parameters across the optimization trajectory.
polyak_averaging.details: For non-convex problems, an exponentially decaying running average is typically used. (p. 322)

pretraining.label: Pretraining
pretraining.summary: Training a simpler model or task before training the final complex model.

greedy_supervised_pretraining.label: Greedy Supervised Pretraining
greedy_supervised_pretraining.summary: Adding layers one by one and training each as a shallow MLP before joint fine-tuning.
greedy_supervised_pretraining.details: Provides better guidance to intermediate levels of a deep hierarchy. (p. 323-324)

fitnets.label: FitNets
fitnets.summary: Using a wide, shallow 'teacher' network to provide 'hints' to a deep, thin 'student' network.
fitnets.details: The student is trained to predict both the final target and the middle layer activations of the teacher. (p. 325)

continuation_methods.label: Continuation Methods
continuation_methods.summary: Constructing a sequence of objective functions J(0)...J(n) that become increasingly difficult.

blurring_objective.label: Objective Blurring
blurring_objective.summary: Smoothing the cost function via sampling to make it approximately convex.
blurring_objective.details: Approximates J(θ) by E[J(θ')] where θ' ~ N(θ, σ²I). This can eliminate flat regions and improve Hessian conditioning. (p. 327)

curriculum_learning.label: Curriculum Learning
curriculum_learning.summary: A form of continuation method where the model is trained on progressively harder examples.

cl_continuation_method.label: Continuation Method
cl_continuation_method.summary: Justification for curriculum learning where earlier cost functions are made easier by increasing the influence of simpler examples via larger coefficients or more frequent sampling. (Bengio et al. 2009)

cl_stochastic_curriculum.label: Stochastic Curriculum
cl_stochastic_curriculum.summary: A strategy for training RNNs to capture long-term dependencies where a random mix of easy and difficult examples is presented, gradually increasing the proportion of difficult examples. Found to be superior to deterministic curricula. (Zaremba and Sutskever 2014)

cnn.label: Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs)
cnn.summary: Specialized neural networks for processing data with a known, grid-like topology (e.g., 1D time-series, 2D images) using convolution instead of general matrix multiplication.

cnn_operation.label: The Convolution Operation
cnn_operation.summary: A mathematical operation on two functions (input and kernel) that produces a feature map.

conv_continuous.label: Continuous Convolution
conv_continuous.summary: Defined as the integral s(t) = integral of x(t-a)w(a)da, where x is the input and w is the weighting function (kernel). (Page 331)

conv_discrete.label: Discrete Convolution
conv_discrete.summary: Defined as s(t) = sum from a=-inf to inf of x(t-a)w(a). Used when time or space is discretized. (Page 331)

conv_tensors.label: Convolutional Tensors
conv_tensors.summary: In machine learning, input and kernels are represented as multi-dimensional arrays called tensors. (Page 331)

conv_commutativity.label: Commutativity in Convolution
conv_commutativity.summary: Convolution is commutative (I * K = K * I), which requires flipping the kernel relative to the input. (Page 332)

conv_cross_correlation.label: Cross-Correlation
conv_cross_correlation.summary: An operation identical to convolution but without flipping the kernel. Most ML libraries implement cross-correlation but call it convolution. (Page 332)

conv_matrix_view.label: Convolution as Matrix Multiplication
conv_matrix_view.summary: Discrete convolution can be viewed as multiplication by a sparse matrix. 1D convolution corresponds to a Toeplitz matrix; 2D corresponds to a doubly block circulant matrix. (Page 333)

cnn_motivation.label: Motivation for Convolution
cnn_motivation.summary: Three core ideas that improve efficiency and performance over dense networks.

mot_sparse_interactions.label: Sparse Interactions
mot_sparse_interactions.summary: Achieved by making the kernel smaller than the input. Reduces memory requirements and computational runtime from O(m*n) to O(k*n), where k is the kernel size. (Page 335)

mot_parameter_sharing.label: Parameter Sharing (Tied Weights)
mot_parameter_sharing.summary: The same kernel parameters are used at every position of the input, drastically reducing storage requirements to k parameters instead of m*n. (Page 337)

mot_equivariance.label: Equivariance to Translation
mot_equivariance.summary: A function f is equivariant to g if f(g(x)) = g(f(x)). Convolutional layers are equivariant to translation (shifting the input shifts the output identically). (Page 338)

cnn_pooling.label: Pooling
cnn_pooling.summary: An operation that replaces the output of the net at a certain location with a summary statistic of nearby outputs.

pool_types.label: Pooling Functions
pool_types.summary: Common types include Max Pooling (maximum value in neighborhood), Average Pooling, L2 norm, or weighted averages based on distance. (Page 339)

pool_invariance.label: Translation Invariance
pool_invariance.summary: Pooling makes representations approximately invariant to small translations of the input; it cares if a feature is present more than exactly where it is. (Page 342)

pool_efficiency.label: Computational Efficiency
pool_efficiency.summary: Reporting summary statistics for pooling regions spaced k pixels apart (striding) reduces the number of inputs for the next layer, improving efficiency. (Page 342)

pool_variable_size.label: Handling Variable Input Size
pool_variable_size.summary: Pooling can be used to map variable-sized inputs to a fixed-size output (e.g., by varying the offset between pooling regions). (Page 342)

cnn_prior.label: Convolution as an Infinitely Strong Prior
cnn_prior.summary: Viewing CNNs as fully connected nets with an infinitely strong prior that forces weights to be zero outside a local receptive field and identical across shifted positions.

prior_underfitting.label: Underfitting Risk
prior_underfitting.summary: Convolution/pooling priors can cause underfitting if the task requires preserving precise spatial information or incorporating distant interactions. (Page 346)

cnn_variants.label: Convolutional Variants
cnn_variants.summary: Modifications to the basic convolution function for different use cases.

var_strided.label: Strided Convolution
var_strided.summary: Skipping over positions of the kernel to downsample the output, reducing computational cost. (Page 348)

var_padding.label: Zero Padding
var_padding.summary: Implicitly adding zeroes to the input boundary. Valid (no padding), Same (output size = input size), Full (every pixel visited k times). (Page 349)

var_locally_connected.label: Locally Connected Layers
var_locally_connected.summary: Similar to convolution in connectivity but without parameter sharing; every connection has its own weight. Useful when features are location-specific (e.g., mouth at bottom of face). (Page 352)

var_tiled.label: Tiled Convolution
var_tiled.summary: A compromise between convolution and locally connected layers; it rotates through a set of t kernels as it moves through space. (Page 352)

cnn_training.label: Training Convolutional Networks
cnn_training.summary: Technical aspects of computing gradients and reconstructing data in CNNs.

train_gradients.label: Convolutional Gradients
train_gradients.summary: Training requires computing gradients with respect to the kernel (weights) and the input (to backpropagate to previous layers). (Page 357)

train_transpose_conv.label: Transpose Convolution
train_transpose_conv.summary: Multiplication by the transpose of the convolution matrix. Essential for reconstructing visible units from hidden units in autoencoders. (Page 356)

cnn_neuroscience.label: Neuroscientific Basis for CNNs
cnn_neuroscience.summary: Design principles derived from the mammalian visual system, specifically V1 (primary visual cortex).

neuro_simple_cells.label: Simple Cells
neuro_simple_cells.summary: Neurons in V1 that respond to specific patterns of light in small, spatially localized receptive fields; emulated by CNN detector units. (Page 365)

neuro_complex_cells.label: Complex Cells
neuro_complex_cells.summary: Neurons in V1 that respond to similar features as simple cells but are invariant to small shifts in position; emulated by CNN pooling units. (Page 365)

neuro_grandmother_cells.label: Grandmother Cells
neuro_grandmother_cells.summary: High-level neurons (e.g., in the medial temporal lobe) that activate for a specific concept regardless of transformation. (Page 365)

neuro_gabor.label: Gabor Functions
neuro_gabor.summary: The weights of V1 simple cells are often described by Gabor functions: a Gaussian gating term multiplied by a cosine function to detect specific spatial frequencies and orientations. (Page 368)

rnn.label: Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs)
rnn.summary: Specialized neural networks for processing sequential data by sharing parameters across time steps.

rnn_unfolding.label: Unfolding Computational Graphs
rnn_unfolding.summary: The process of mapping a recurrent circuit into a directed acyclic graph by repeating the transition function f for each time step τ. (Page 375)

unfold_advantages.label: Advantages of Unfolding
unfold_advantages.summary: 1. Fixed input size regardless of sequence length. 2. Ability to share the same transition function and parameters at every time step. (Page 377)

rnn_architecture.label: RNN Architecture
rnn_architecture.summary: Standard RNN components and their mathematical representation.

arch_hidden_state.label: Hidden State h(t)
arch_hidden_state.summary: The state at time t, computed as h(t) = f(h(t-1), x(t); theta), acting as a lossy summary of the past sequence. (Page 376)

arch_turing_complete.label: Turing Completeness
arch_turing_complete.summary: RNNs are universal in the sense that any function computable by a Turing machine can be computed by an RNN of finite size. (Page 379)

train_bptt.label: Back-propagation Through Time (BPTT)
train_bptt.summary: The application of the generalized back-propagation algorithm to the unrolled computational graph. Runtime and memory cost are O(tau). (Page 381)

train_teacher_forcing.label: Teacher Forcing
train_teacher_forcing.summary: A training technique where the model receives the ground truth output y(t) as input at time t+1 instead of its own prediction o(t). (Page 382)

rnn_bidirectional.label: Bidirectional RNNs
rnn_bidirectional.summary: RNNs that combine a forward-moving sub-RNN and a backward-moving sub-RNN, allowing the output at time t to depend on both the past and the future. (Page 394)

rnn_seq2seq.label: Encoder-Decoder (Seq2Seq) Architecture
rnn_seq2seq.summary: An architecture consisting of an Encoder RNN that produces a fixed-size context vector C, and a Decoder RNN that generates an output sequence of variable length. (Page 396)

rnn_deep.label: Deep Recurrent Networks
rnn_deep.summary: RNNs that introduce depth by stacking multiple layers of hidden states or using deep MLPs for input-to-hidden, hidden-to-hidden, and hidden-to-output transformations. (Page 397)

core_rnn.label: Recurrent and Recursive Networks
core_rnn.summary: Neural network architectures designed for sequential or hierarchical data processing.

sub_rnn_depth.label: RNN Depth and Structure
sub_rnn_depth.summary: Methods to increase the computational depth of recurrent networks.

fact_mlp_transition.label: MLP Transitions
fact_mlp_transition.summary: Using an MLP for state-to-state transitions doubles the length of the shortest path between variables in different time steps compared to ordinary RNNs (p. 398).

fact_skip_connections_depth.label: Path-Lengthening Mitigation
fact_skip_connections_depth.summary: Skip connections in the hidden-to-hidden path can mitigate the path-lengthening effect caused by deeper computation (p. 399).

sub_recursive_nets.label: Recursive Neural Networks
sub_recursive_nets.summary: Generalizations of recurrent networks where the computational graph is a tree rather than a chain.

fact_rec_tree_structure.label: Tree-Based Computation
fact_rec_tree_structure.summary: Maps variable-size sequences to fixed-size representations using a fixed set of parameters (U, V, W) (p. 400).

fact_rec_complexity.label: Computational Depth Reduction
fact_rec_complexity.summary: For a sequence of length tau, depth is reduced from tau in RNNs to O(log tau) in recursive nets, helping with long-term dependencies (p. 400).

fact_rec_tree_options.label: Tree Structuring Strategies
fact_rec_tree_options.summary: Trees can be data-independent (balanced binary), fixed by external methods (NLP parse trees), or inferred by the learner (p. 400).

sub_long_term_dependencies.label: The Challenge of Long-Term Dependencies
sub_long_term_dependencies.summary: The difficulty of learning interactions between distant time steps due to gradient instability.

fact_grad_vanishing_exploding.label: Vanishing and Exploding Gradients
fact_grad_vanishing_exploding.summary: Gradients propagated over many stages tend to vanish (common) or explode (rare but damaging), making long-term interactions exponentially smaller than short-term ones (p. 401).

fact_eigenvalue_decay.label: Mathematical Cause of Gradient Instability
fact_eigenvalue_decay.summary: In a simple recurrence h(t) = W^t h(0), eigenvalues of W with magnitude < 1 decay to zero, while those > 1 explode (p. 402).

fact_dynamical_systems_view.label: RNNs as Dynamical Systems
fact_dynamical_systems_view.summary: To store memories robustly, RNNs must enter regions of parameter space where gradients vanish (p. 403).

sub_reservoir_computing.label: Reservoir Computing
sub_reservoir_computing.summary: Architectures that fix recurrent weights and only train the output layer.

fact_esn_definition.label: Echo State Networks (ESN)
fact_esn_definition.summary: Set recurrent weights to capture history and learn only the output weights via linear regression (p. 403).

fact_spectral_radius.label: Spectral Radius in ESNs
fact_spectral_radius.summary: The maximum absolute value of the eigenvalues of the Jacobian J(t). If rho < 1, the system is contractive; if rho > 1, it may explode unless stabilized by nonlinearities (p. 404-405).

fact_contractive_maps.label: Contractive Mapping
fact_contractive_maps.summary: When the spectral radius is < 1, a small change becomes smaller after each time step, causing the network to forget the past (p. 405).

sub_time_scales.label: Strategies for Multiple Time Scales
sub_time_scales.summary: Designing models that operate at both fine-grained and coarse-grained time scales.

fact_skip_connections_time.label: Temporal Skip Connections
fact_skip_connections_time.summary: Connections with time-delay 'd' mitigate vanishing gradients by making them diminish as a function of tau/d rather than tau (p. 406).

fact_leaky_units.label: Leaky Units
fact_leaky_units.summary: Units with linear self-connections (weight alpha near 1) that act like running averages to remember information over long durations (p. 407).

fact_removing_connections.label: Connection Removal
fact_removing_connections.summary: Actively removing length-one connections and replacing them with longer ones forces units to operate on a long time scale (p. 407).

sub_gated_rnns.label: Gated RNNs
sub_gated_rnns.summary: Networks that use gates to dynamically control the flow and forgetting of information.

sub_lstm.label: Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM)
sub_lstm.summary: A gated architecture designed to maintain a constant error flow through a state unit.

fact_lstm_components.label: LSTM Cell Components
fact_lstm_components.summary: Consists of a state unit s(t), input gate g(t), forget gate f(t), and output gate q(t) (p. 409-410).

fact_lstm_forget_gate.label: The Forget Gate
fact_lstm_forget_gate.summary: A sigmoid unit that sets the weight of the state's linear self-loop to a value between 0 and 1, allowing the network to learn when to clear the state (p. 410).

sub_gru.label: Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU)
sub_gru.summary: A simplified gated RNN where a single unit controls both forgetting and updating.

fact_gru_gates.label: GRU Update and Reset Gates
fact_gru_gates.summary: The update gate u(t) acts as a conditional leaky integrator; the reset gate r(t) controls which parts of the state are used to compute the next target state (p. 411-412).

sub_explicit_memory.label: Explicit Memory
sub_explicit_memory.summary: Architectures that decouple representation (task network) from storage (memory cells).

fact_ntm_definition.label: Neural Turing Machine (NTM)
fact_ntm_definition.summary: Learns to read from and write arbitrary content to memory cells via a content-based soft attention mechanism without explicit supervision (p. 417-418).

fact_addressing_mechanisms.label: Content-based vs Location-based Addressing
fact_addressing_mechanisms.summary: Content-based addressing retrieves memory based on a matching pattern (analogous to recalling lyrics); location-based addressing refers to a specific slot (p. 418).

core_practical_methodology.label: Practical Methodology
core_practical_methodology.summary: The systematic process of designing, monitoring, and debugging machine learning systems.

sub_performance_metrics.label: Performance Metrics
sub_performance_metrics.summary: Defining the success criteria for a model beyond the training cost function.

fact_bayes_error.label: Bayes Error
fact_bayes_error.summary: The minimum error rate achievable even with infinite data, due to stochasticity or incomplete input features (p. 422).

fact_precision_recall.label: Precision and Recall
fact_precision_recall.summary: Precision is the fraction of reported detections that were correct; Recall is the fraction of true events detected. F-score is their harmonic mean (p. 423).

fact_coverage_metric.label: Coverage
fact_coverage_metric.summary: The fraction of examples for which a system produces a response; often traded against accuracy (p. 423).

sub_baseline_models.label: Default Baseline Models
sub_baseline_models.summary: Recommended starting points for various data structures.

fact_baseline_selection.label: Model Selection Guide
fact_baseline_selection.summary: Fixed vectors -> Feedforward; Topological/Images -> CNN; Sequences -> Gated RNN (LSTM/GRU) (p. 425).

sub_data_gathering.label: Determining Data Needs
sub_data_gathering.summary: Analyzing training vs test performance to decide if more data is required.

fact_data_gap_analysis.label: Train-Test Gap
fact_data_gap_analysis.summary: If training error is high -> increase model size or tune optimization. If test error is much higher than training error -> gather more data or improve regularization (p. 426).

sub_hyperparameter_tuning.label: Hyperparameter Optimization
