sub_hyperparameter_tuning.summary: Strategies for adjusting the effective capacity of a model.

fact_learning_rate_importance.label: Learning Rate
fact_learning_rate_importance.summary: The most critical hyperparameter; too high causes instability, too low causes slow training or stagnation (p. 429).

fact_grid_vs_random_search.label: Grid vs Random Search
fact_grid_vs_random_search.summary: Grid search is exponential in number of hyperparameters. Random search is more efficient because it explores unique values of influential hyperparameters on nearly every trial (p. 433-434).

fact_bayesian_optimization.label: Model-Based (Bayesian) Optimization
fact_bayesian_optimization.summary: Uses a regression model to estimate validation error and uncertainty, balancing exploration and exploitation (p. 435).

sub_debugging_strategies.label: Debugging Strategies
sub_debugging_strategies.summary: Methods to distinguish between algorithmic failure and software bugs.

fact_debug_tiny_dataset.label: Fitting a Tiny Dataset
fact_debug_tiny_dataset.summary: If a model cannot overfit a single example, there is likely a software defect preventing optimization (p. 438).

fact_debug_numerical_grad.label: Numerical Gradient Checking
fact_debug_numerical_grad.summary: Comparing automatic differentiation results with finite differences (f(x+eps) - f(x))/eps to verify gradient implementation (p. 438-439).

core_infrastructure_apps.label: Large-Scale Infrastructure and Applications
core_infrastructure_apps.summary: The hardware, software, and application-specific strategies for deploying deep learning.

sub_hardware_impl.label: Hardware Implementations
sub_hardware_impl.summary: Comparative advantages of different processing units.

fact_gpu_advantages.label: GPU Performance Characteristics
fact_gpu_advantages.summary: High memory bandwidth and massive parallelism for simple, non-branching operations (matrix multiplication) (p. 444).

fact_gpu_warps.label: GPU Warps and Branching
fact_gpu_warps.summary: Threads are divided into warps; if threads in a warp take different code paths, they must be traversed sequentially, making branching expensive (p. 445).

fact_specialized_hardware.label: Specialized hardware
fact_specialized_hardware.summary: Includes ASICs, FPGAs, and low-precision (8-16 bit) fixed-point implementations to reduce power and surface area (p. 451).

fact_data_vs_model_parallelism.label: Parallelism Types
fact_data_vs_model_parallelism.summary: Data parallelism: each machine processes different examples. Model parallelism: machines work together on one example, each running a part of the model (p. 446).

fact_async_sgd.label: Asynchronous SGD
fact_async_sgd.summary: Cores read parameters without locks and increment them independently, increasing the production rate of steps (p. 446).

sub_model_optimization.label: Model Optimization and Dynamic Structure
sub_model_optimization.summary: Reducing inference cost and increasing efficiency.

fact_model_compression.label: Model Compression
fact_model_compression.summary: Replacing a large, over-parameterized model (used to prevent overfitting) with a smaller model trained to match the original's function f(x) (p. 447).

fact_conditional_computation.label: Conditional Computation
fact_conditional_computation.summary: Determining which subset of features or networks to compute given the input to reduce total operations (p. 448).

fact_cascade_classifiers.label: Cascade of Classifiers
fact_cascade_classifiers.summary: A sequence of classifiers where early models have low capacity and high recall, and later models have high precision; examples are rejected early to save cost (p. 448).

sub_cv_apps.label: Computer Vision Applications
sub_cv_apps.summary: Preprocessing and augmentation for image-based tasks.

fact_gcn.label: Global Contrast Normalization (GCN)
fact_gcn.summary: Subtracts the mean and rescales the image so the standard deviation equals a constant s, mapping examples to a spherical shell (p. 454).

fact_lcn.label: Local Contrast Normalization (LCN)
fact_lcn.summary: Normalizes contrast across small windows, highlighting edges and corners by removing regions of constant intensity (p. 456).

fact_dataset_augmentation.label: Dataset Augmentation
fact_dataset_augmentation.summary: Increasing training set size via transformations like random translations, rotations, flips, and color perturbations to improve generalization (p. 457).

asr.label: Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR)
asr.summary: The domain of converting spoken language into text, transitioning from traditional GMM-HMM to deep learning architectures.

gmm_hmm.label: GMM-HMM Technology
gmm_hmm.summary: Traditional speech recognition technology based on Gaussian Mixture Models and Hidden Markov Models.

gmm_hmm_stagnation.label: GMM-HMM Performance Plateau
gmm_hmm_stagnation.summary: A period of roughly ten years where error rates did not improve significantly despite larger training sets (p. 460).

asr_deep_learning.label: Deep Learning in ASR
asr_deep_learning.summary: The shift towards neural networks to improve speech recognition accuracy.

cnn_asr.label: Convolutional Networks for ASR
cnn_asr.summary: Models that treat the input spectrogram as an image with axes for time and frequency, replicating weights across both (p. 460).

tdnn_asr.label: Time-Delay Neural Networks (TDNN)
tdnn_asr.summary: Earlier ASR networks that replicated weights only across the time dimension (p. 460).

end_to_end_asr.label: End-to-End ASR Systems
end_to_end_asr.summary: Systems that completely remove the Hidden Markov Model (HMM) for direct mapping.

lstm_ctc_asr.label: LSTM-RNN with CTC
lstm_ctc_asr.summary: Use of deep LSTM RNNs within the Connectionist Temporal Classification (CTC) framework for frame-to-phoneme alignment, achieving a TIMIT phoneme error rate of 17.7% (p. 460).

rnn_depth_definition.label: Deep RNN Depth
rnn_depth_definition.summary: Deep RNNs possess two types of depth: ordinary depth from a stack of layers and depth due to time unfolding (p. 460).

acoustic_phonetic_alignment.label: Acoustic-Phonetic Alignment
acoustic_phonetic_alignment.summary: Learning to align acoustic-level information directly with phonetic-level information (p. 460).

nlp.label: Natural Language Processing (NLP)
nlp.summary: The use of human languages by computers, involving the processing of ambiguous and non-formal descriptions.

language_models.label: Language Models
language_models.summary: Models that define a probability distribution over sequences of tokens (words, characters, or bytes) (p. 461).

n_grams.label: n-grams
n_grams.summary: Models based on fixed-length sequences of n tokens to define conditional probabilities of the n-th token given the preceding n-1 tokens (p. 461).

ngram_types.label: n-gram Terminology
ngram_types.summary: n=1: unigram; n=2: bigram; n=3: trigram (p. 462).

ngram_mle.label: Maximum Likelihood Estimate (MLE) for n-grams
ngram_mle.summary: Computed simply by counting occurrences of each possible n-gram in the training set (p. 461).

ngram_smoothing.label: n-gram Smoothing
ngram_smoothing.summary: Techniques to avoid zero probabilities when tuples appear in test sets but not training sets (p. 462).

smoothing_bayesian.label: Bayesian Smoothing
smoothing_bayesian.summary: Adding non-zero probability mass to all possible next symbols, justified as Bayesian inference with a uniform or Dirichlet prior (p. 462).

smoothing_mixture.label: Mixture Model Smoothing
smoothing_mixture.summary: Combining higher-order n-grams (capacity) with lower-order n-grams (to avoid zero counts) (p. 462).

smoothing_backoff.label: Back-off Methods
smoothing_backoff.summary: Looking up lower-order n-grams if the frequency of the higher-order context is too small (p. 462).

ngram_curse_dim.label: Curse of Dimensionality in n-grams
ngram_curse_dim.summary: Large vocabulary sizes lead to massive sparse discrete spaces where most n-grams never occur in training, making them behave like local non-parametric predictors (p. 463).

class_based_lm.label: Class-based Language Models
class_based_lm.summary: Partitioning words into clusters/classes based on co-occurrence to share statistical strength between semantically similar words (p. 463).

nlms.label: Neural Language Models (NLMs)
nlms.summary: Models using distributed representations (embeddings) to overcome the curse of dimensionality by sharing statistical strength (p. 464).

word_embeddings.label: Word Embeddings
word_embeddings.summary: Mapping raw symbols from a high-dimensional one-hot space into a lower-dimensional feature space where semantically similar words are neighbors (p. 464).

high_dim_outputs.label: High-Dimensional Outputs in NLP
high_dim_outputs.summary: The computational challenge of performing softmax over vocabularies containing hundreds of thousands of words (p. 465).

short_list_approach.label: Short List Approach
short_list_approach.summary: Splitting vocabulary V into a shortlist L (most frequent, handled by neural net) and a tail T (rare words, handled by n-gram model) (p. 466).

hierarchical_softmax.label: Hierarchical Softmax
hierarchical_softmax.summary: Decomposing probability distributions into a balanced tree of categories, reducing complexity from O(|V|) to O(log |V|) (p. 467).

importance_sampling_nlp.label: Importance Sampling for NLMs
importance_sampling_nlp.summary: Estimating the negative phase of the gradient using a proposal distribution q instead of the model's own distribution to avoid computing all scores (p. 470).

biased_importance_sampling.label: Biased Importance Sampling
biased_importance_sampling.summary: Normalizing importance weights to sum to 1 when using a proposal distribution q (p. 470).

nce_ranking_loss.label: NCE and Ranking Loss
nce_ranking_loss.summary: Ranking loss maximizes the score of the correct word relative to others; Noise-Contrastive Estimation (NCE) is another alternative to reduce output cost (p. 471).

nmt.label: Neural Machine Translation (NMT)
nmt.summary: The task of translating text from one language to another using neural networks.

encoder_decoder_nmt.label: Encoder-Decoder Architecture
encoder_decoder_nmt.summary: An encoder reads the source sequence to produce a context C (summary), and a decoder generates the target sentence from C (p. 474).

attention_mechanism.label: Attention Mechanism
attention_mechanism.summary: A weighted average of feature vectors from the source, allowing the decoder to focus on different parts of the input sentence at each time step (p. 475).

recsys.label: Recommender Systems
recsys.summary: Systems predicting associations between users and items, used in online advertising and product recommendations.

collaborative_filtering.label: Collaborative Filtering
collaborative_filtering.summary: Generalizing based on the similarity between user preference patterns. Often uses bilinear prediction (dot product of embeddings) or SVD (p. 479).

content_based_recsys.label: Content-Based Recommender Systems
content_based_recsys.summary: Solving the 'cold-start' problem by using extra information (user profiles or item features) rather than just ID history (p. 480).

exploration_exploitation.label: Exploration vs. Exploitation
exploration_exploitation.summary: A reinforcement learning trade-off: exploitation uses the current best policy, while exploration tries new actions to gather data (p. 481).

contextual_bandits.label: Contextual Bandits
contextual_bandits.summary: A special case of RL where a single action is taken based on a context variable and a single reward is observed (p. 481).

knowledge_rep.label: Knowledge Representation and QA
knowledge_rep.summary: Representing facts and relations between entities to enable reasoning and question answering.

knowledge_bases.label: Knowledge Bases
knowledge_bases.summary: Databases of commonsense or expert knowledge stored as triplets: (subject, relation, object) (p. 483).

link_prediction.label: Link Prediction
link_prediction.summary: Predicting missing arcs in a knowledge graph to generalize new facts from old ones (p. 484).

memory_networks.label: Memory Networks
memory_networks.summary: Architectures using an explicit memory mechanism to remember and retrieve declarative facts for QA tasks (p. 484).

linear_factor_models.label: Linear Factor Models
linear_factor_models.summary: Probabilistic models with latent variables h and a linear decoder x = Wh + b + noise (p. 489).

ppca_fa.label: Probabilistic PCA and Factor Analysis
ppca_fa.summary: LFM variants; Factor Analysis uses diagonal covariance noise; PPCA uses isotropic noise (p. 490).

ica.label: Independent Component Analysis (ICA)
ica.summary: Modeling linear factors to separate mixed signals into independent, non-Gaussian components (p. 491).

nice_ica.label: NICE (Nonlinear ICA)
nice_ica.summary: A nonlinear extension of ICA using stacks of invertible transformations with efficiently computable Jacobian determinants (p. 492).

sfa.label: Slow Feature Analysis (SFA)
sfa.summary: LFM that learns invariant features based on the 'slowness principle': important characteristics change slowly over time (p. 493).

sparse_coding.label: Sparse Coding
sparse_coding.summary: A model utilizing a linear decoder and a prior p(h) with sharp peaks near 0 (e.g., Laplace), requiring non-parametric iterative encoding (p. 496).

autoencoders.label: Autoencoders
autoencoders.summary: Neural networks trained to copy input to output via a hidden code h, consisting of an encoder f and a decoder g (p. 502).

undercomplete_ae.label: Undercomplete Autoencoders
undercomplete_ae.summary: Autoencoders where the code dimension is smaller than the input dimension, forcing the capture of salient features (p. 503).

regularized_ae.label: Regularized Autoencoders
regularized_ae.summary: Autoencoders using loss functions to encourage sparsity, robustness, or small derivatives to prevent learning the trivial identity function (p. 504).

sparse_ae.label: Sparse Autoencoders
sparse_ae.summary: AEs using a sparsity penalty Omega(h) on the code layer, often interpreted as a latent variable prior (p. 505).

denoising_ae.label: Denoising Autoencoders (DAE)
denoising_ae.summary: AEs trained to reconstruct clean data x from corrupted input x_tilde, effectively learning the score of the data distribution (p. 507).

score_matching_dae.label: Score Matching in DAE
score_matching_dae.summary: The training criterion of DAEs allows them to estimate the score (gradient of log p_data) (p. 513).

contractive_ae.label: Contractive Autoencoders (CAE)
contractive_ae.summary: AEs using a penalty on the Frobenius norm of the Jacobian of the encoder to resist infinitesimal perturbations (p. 521).

manifold_learning_ae.label: Manifold Learning with Autoencoders
manifold_learning_ae.summary: The use of AEs to learn the structure of low-dimensional manifolds, where the encoder is sensitive only to changes tangent to the manifold (p. 516).

semantic_hashing.label: Semantic Hashing
semantic_hashing.summary: The process of producing binary codes for semantic hashing using encoding functions.

sh_encoding_function.label: Semantic Hashing Encoding Function
sh_encoding_function.summary: Typically uses sigmoids on the final layer to produce binary codes.

sh_saturation_trick.label: Sigmoid Saturation Technique
sh_saturation_trick.summary: Training sigmoid units to be saturated nearly 0 or 1 by injecting additive noise before the nonlinearity during training, increasing noise magnitude over time to force the network to increase input magnitude (p. 525).

representation_learning_core.label: Representation Learning
representation_learning_core.summary: The study of how information is represented to make subsequent learning tasks easier.

rl_definition.label: Definition of Representation Learning
rl_definition.summary: A good representation is one that makes a subsequent learning task easier. The choice depends on the task (e.g., Arabic numerals facilitate long division more than Roman numerals) (p. 526).

rl_supervised.label: Supervised Representation Learning
rl_supervised.summary: Feedforward networks where the last layer is a linear classifier (e.g., softmax) and previous layers learn representations that make the classification task easier (e.g., making classes linearly separable) (p. 526).

rl_unsupervised.label: Unsupervised Representation Learning
rl_unsupervised.summary: Algorithms designed to shape representations explicitly, such as encouraging independence between elements of the representation vector h to ease density estimation (p. 526).

rl_semi_supervised.label: Semi-Supervised Representation Learning
rl_semi_supervised.summary: Using large amounts of unlabeled data to learn a good representation, which then resolves overfitting when applying supervised learning to small labeled datasets (p. 527).

greedy_pretraining.label: Greedy Layer-Wise Unsupervised Pretraining
greedy_pretraining.summary: A procedure where layers are trained one at a time using unsupervised algorithms to find a good initialization for joint supervised training.

gp_mechanism.label: Pretraining Mechanism
gp_mechanism.summary: Uses single-layer algorithms (RBM, autoencoder, sparse coding) to produce a new representation of the data layer by layer. It acts as a regularizer and parameter initialization (p. 528).

gp_terminology.label: Pretraining Terminology
gp_terminology.summary: Greedy: optimizes pieces independently; Layer-wise: independent pieces are layers; Unsupervised: uses unsupervised algorithms; Pretraining: initial step before joint fine-tuning (p. 528).

gp_benefits.label: Benefits of Pretraining
gp_benefits.summary: Can reduce test error by taking parameters into regions otherwise inaccessible, reducing the variance of the estimation process (p. 530, 533). Especially useful when initial representations are poor (e.g., one-hot word vectors) or labeled data is scarce (p. 531).

gp_limitations.label: Limitations of Pretraining
gp_limitations.summary: Two separate training phases lead to complex hyperparameter tuning. Often outperformed by simultaneous supervised/unsupervised learning or modern techniques like Batch Norm/Dropout on medium-large datasets (p. 534, 535).

transfer_learning_domain.label: Transfer Learning and Domain Adaptation
transfer_learning_domain.summary: Exploiting knowledge learned in one setting (P1) to improve generalization in another setting (P2).

tl_transfer_learning.label: Transfer Learning
tl_transfer_learning.summary: Performing multiple tasks where factors explaining variations in P1 are relevant to P2. Often involves shared lower layers (representation) and task-specific upper layers (p. 536).

tl_domain_adaptation.label: Domain Adaptation
tl_domain_adaptation.summary: The task and mapping remain the same, but the input distribution differs (e.g., sentiment analysis for books vs. electronics) (p. 536).

tl_concept_drift.label: Concept Drift
tl_concept_drift.summary: A form of transfer learning resulting from gradual changes in the data distribution over time (p. 537).

tl_one_shot.label: One-Shot Learning
tl_one_shot.summary: Generalizing to a new task using only one labeled example, enabled by representations that cleanly separate underlying classes (p. 538).

tl_zero_shot.label: Zero-Shot Learning
tl_zero_shot.summary: Also called zero-data learning; performing a task with no labeled examples by utilizing a task description T and distributed representations (e.g., word embeddings) to relate modalities (p. 538, 539).

causal_disentanglement.label: Semi-Supervised Disentangling of Causal Factors
causal_disentanglement.summary: The hypothesis that an ideal representation disentangles the underlying causes of the observed data.

cd_salience.label: Saliency in Representation
cd_salience.summary: The criteria for what is encoded. Mean Squared Error (MSE) may fail to encode small but critical objects (e.g., a ping pong ball in robotics) because they don't significantly change pixel brightness (p. 543).

cd_gan_salience.label: Adversarial Salience
cd_gan_salience.summary: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) identify salience based on patterns a classifier can recognize, allowing the model to capture details like ears on a face that MSE would ignore (p. 544).

cd_robustness.label: Causal Robustness
cd_robustness.summary: Modeling p(x|y) (where y is cause and x is effect) is more robust to changes in p(y) than modeling p(y|x) (p. 545).

distributed_representations.label: Distributed Representations
distributed_representations.summary: Representations where concepts are composed of many elements that can be set separately.

dr_power.label: Power of Distributed Representations
dr_power.summary: Can describe k^n different concepts using n features with k values, offering exponential capacity compared to symbolic representations (p. 546).

dr_vs_symbolic.label: Distributed vs Symbolic (One-Hot)
dr_vs_symbolic.summary: Symbolic representations associate an input with a single category. Distributed representations allow for shared attributes (e.g., 'has_fur' for both cats and dogs), enabling better generalization (p. 546, 548).

dr_geometry.label: Geometric Interpretation
dr_geometry.summary: A distributed representation with n linear-threshold features in Rd distinguishes O(n^d) regions in input space (p. 550).

dr_generalization.label: Distributed Generalization
dr_generalization.summary: Generalization is possible because semantic similarity corresponds to distance in the representation space. Capacity is limited by the VC dimension of the classifier, encouraging linear separability of classes (p. 550).

depth_efficiency.label: Exponential Gains from Depth
depth_efficiency.summary: The use of deep hierarchies of nonlinearities to increase statistical efficiency.

de_universal_approximation.label: Universal Approximation and Depth
de_universal_approximation.summary: While single-hidden-layer networks are universal approximators, deep architectures can represent certain families of functions with exponentially fewer units (p. 553).

de_statistical_efficiency.label: Statistical Efficiency of Depth
de_statistical_efficiency.summary: Deep distributed representations allow high-level factors to be obtained through the composition of many nonlinearities, boosting efficiency over shallow networks (p. 553).

structured_probabilistic_models.label: Structured Probabilistic Models
structured_probabilistic_models.summary: The use of graphs to represent probability distributions and their interactions.

spm_directed.label: Directed Graphical Models (Bayesian Networks)
spm_directed.summary: Models where edges are arrows indicating that the child's distribution is defined conditionally on the parents: p(x) = Π p(xi | Pa(xi)) (p. 563, 564).

spm_undirected.label: Undirected Graphical Models (Markov Random Fields)
spm_undirected.summary: Models where edges are undirected. The unnormalized distribution is the product of clique potentials φ: ˜p(x) = Π φ_C(xC) (p. 566, 567).

spm_partition_function.label: The Partition Function (Z)
spm_partition_function.summary: The normalizing constant Z = ∫ ˜p(x) dx required to turn an unnormalized distribution into a valid probability distribution. In deep learning, Z is usually intractable (p. 568).

spm_ebm.label: Energy-Based Models (EBM)
spm_ebm.summary: Undirected models where ˜p(x) = exp(-E(x)). The energy function E(x) is learned via unconstrained optimization. Common examples include Boltzmann Machines (p. 569, 570).

spm_separation.label: Separation and D-Separation
spm_separation.summary: Techniques to determine conditional independence. Undirected models use 'separation' (blocking paths with observed variables). Directed models use 'd-separation' (handling V-structures/colliders where observing the child activates the path) (p. 572, 574).

spm_conversion.label: Model Conversion
spm_conversion.summary: Moralization converts directed to undirected by connecting parents of a shared child. Triangulation converts undirected to directed by adding chords to loops of length > 3 (p. 577, 578).

spm_factor_graphs.label: Factor Graphs
spm_factor_graphs.summary: Bipartite undirected graphs with variable nodes (circles) and factor nodes (squares) that explicitly define the scope of each φ function, resolving ambiguity in standard undirected graphs (p. 579, 580).

spm_deep_learning_approach.label: Deep Learning Approach to Probabilistic Models
spm_deep_learning_approach.summary: Emphasis on distributed representations, large latent layers, and approximate inference (Variational Inference, Gibbs Sampling) rather than exact inference or loopy belief propagation (p. 585, 586).

rbm.label: Restricted Boltzmann Machines (RBM)
rbm.summary: A type of energy-based model where the graph structure restricts interactions to only exist between visible and hidden layers, not within them.

rbm_structure.label: RBM Structure
rbm_structure.summary: The architectural constraints of an RBM.

rbm_no_intra_layer_interaction.label: No Intra-layer Interactions
rbm_no_intra_layer_interaction.summary: There are no direct interactions between any two visible units or between any two hidden units, distinguishing it from a general Boltzmann machine. (p. 587)

rbm_properties.label: RBM Probabilistic Properties
rbm_properties.summary: The mathematical consequences of the RBM's restricted structure.

rbm_factorial_conditionals.label: Factorial Conditionals
rbm_factorial_conditionals.summary: Due to the structure, the conditional distributions are products of individual conditionals: p(h|v) = Π p(hi|v) and p(v|h) = Π p(vi|h). (p. 587)

rbm_binary_conditionals.label: Binary RBM Conditionals
rbm_binary_conditionals.summary: For binary RBMs, the probability of a hidden unit being 1 is given by the sigmoid σ(v^T W_{:,i} + bi). (p. 587)

rbm_sampling.label: RBM Sampling
rbm_sampling.summary: Methods for generating samples from an RBM.

block_gibbs_sampling.label: Block Gibbs Sampling
block_gibbs_sampling.summary: An efficient sampling method that alternates between sampling all hidden units simultaneously and sampling all visible units simultaneously. (p. 587)

rbm_energy.label: RBM Energy and Training
rbm_energy.summary: The energy function and its use in training.

rbm_energy_derivative.label: Energy Derivative
rbm_energy_derivative.summary: The derivative of the energy function with respect to weights is simple: ∂E(v,h)/∂W_{i,j} = -v_i h_j. (p. 587)

monte_carlo.label: Monte Carlo Methods
monte_carlo.summary: Randomized algorithms used to approximate sums, integrals, and expectations when exact computation is intractable.

randomized_algorithm_types.label: Randomized Algorithm Types
randomized_algorithm_types.summary: The two primary categories of randomized algorithms.

las_vegas_algorithms.label: Las Vegas Algorithms
las_vegas_algorithms.summary: Algorithms that always return the correct answer but consume a random amount of resources (memory/time). (p. 590)

monte_carlo_algorithms.label: Monte Carlo Algorithms
monte_carlo_algorithms.summary: Algorithms that return answers with a random amount of error, which can be reduced by increasing resources. (p. 590)

monte_carlo_basics.label: Basics of Monte Carlo Sampling
monte_carlo_basics.summary: The theoretical foundation of using samples to estimate expectations.

empirical_average.label: Empirical Average
empirical_average.summary: The approximation of an expectation s = E[f(x)] by the average of n samples: ŝ = (1/n) Σ f(x_i). (p. 591)

law_of_large_numbers.label: Law of Large Numbers
law_of_large_numbers.summary: States that if samples x_i are i.i.d., the empirical average converges almost surely to the expected value as n approaches infinity, provided variance is bounded. (p. 591)

central_limit_theorem.label: Central Limit Theorem
central_limit_theorem.summary: States that the distribution of the average ŝ_n converges to a normal distribution with mean s and variance Var[f(x)]/n. (p. 591)

importance_sampling.label: Importance Sampling
importance_sampling.summary: A technique to estimate expectations by sampling from a different distribution q rather than the target distribution p.

importance_sampling_estimator.label: Importance Sampling Estimator
importance_sampling_estimator.summary: The estimator is defined as ŝ_q = (1/n) Σ [p(x_i)f(x_i) / q(x_i)], where x_i are sampled from q. (p. 593)

optimal_importance_distribution.label: Optimal Importance Distribution
optimal_importance_distribution.summary: The distribution q* that minimizes variance is q*(x) ∝ p(x)|f(x)|. (p. 593)

mcmc.label: Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC)
mcmc.summary: A family of algorithms that use Markov chains to approximately sample from a distribution p(x), especially useful for Energy-Based Models (EBMs).

markov_chain_definition.label: Markov Chain Definition
markov_chain_definition.summary: Defined by a random state x and a transition distribution T(x'|x). Running the chain means repeatedly updating x based on T. (p. 595)

mcmc_theory.label: MCMC Convergence Theory
mcmc_theory.summary: The mathematical basis for the convergence of Markov chains to a stationary distribution.

stochastic_matrix.label: Stochastic Matrix
stochastic_matrix.summary: A matrix A where each column represents a probability distribution, describing the transition operator of the Markov chain. (p. 596)

perron_frobenius_theorem.label: Perron-Frobenius Theorem
perron_frobenius_theorem.summary: Guarantees that for a stochastic matrix, the largest eigenvalue is 1. (p. 596)

stationary_distribution.label: Stationary Distribution
stationary_distribution.summary: The equilibrium distribution v* where Av* = v*. Once reached, the distribution over states remains unchanged by the transition operator. (p. 597)

gibbs_sampling.label: Gibbs Sampling
gibbs_sampling.summary: A specific MCMC method where sampling is performed by selecting one variable x_i and sampling it from p(x_i | neighbors). (p. 599)

block_gibbs_sampling_mcmc.label: Block Gibbs Sampling
block_gibbs_sampling_mcmc.summary: Updating multiple conditionally independent variables simultaneously to improve efficiency. (p. 599)

mixing_problems.label: MCMC Mixing Problems
mixing_problems.summary: Difficulties in MCMC where the chain fails to visit all modes of the distribution efficiently.

slow_mixing.label: Slow Mixing
slow_mixing.summary: Occurs when samples become highly correlated and the chain stays within a single mode for too long. (p. 600)

energy_barriers.label: Energy Barriers
energy_barriers.summary: Regions of low probability (high energy) between modes that make transitions between modes exponentially unlikely. (p. 600)

mixing_time.label: Mixing Time
mixing_time.summary: The time required for a Markov chain to reach its equilibrium distribution; determined by the magnitude of the second largest eigenvalue of the transition matrix. (p. 598)

tempering.label: Tempering
tempering.summary: Techniques to accelerate mixing by modifying the distribution's sharpness.

temperature_parameter.label: Temperature Parameter (beta)
temperature_parameter.summary: The reciprocal of temperature beta controls the distribution's peakiness: p_beta(x) ∝ exp(-beta E(x)). beta=0 is uniform, beta=infinity is deterministic. (p. 603)

parallel_tempering.label: Parallel Tempering
parallel_tempering.summary: Simulating multiple chains at different temperatures and stochastically swapping states between them to escape local modes. (p. 603)

partition_function.label: Confronting the Partition Function
partition_function.summary: Methods for training undirected models where the normalization constant Z(theta) is intractable.

log_likelihood_gradient.label: Log-Likelihood Gradient
log_likelihood_gradient.summary: The gradient of log p(x; theta) decomposes into a positive phase (data) and a negative phase (model samples). (p. 606)

positive_phase.label: Positive Phase
positive_phase.summary: Increasing the unnormalized probability log p_tilde(x) for x drawn from the data distribution. (p. 607)

negative_phase.label: Negative Phase
negative_phase.summary: Decreasing the partition function Z by decreasing log p_tilde(x) for x drawn from the model distribution. (p. 607)

mcmc_approximation_methods.label: MCMC Approximation Methods
mcmc_approximation_methods.summary: Practical algorithms to approximate the negative phase of the gradient.

contrastive_divergence.label: Contrastive Divergence (CD)
contrastive_divergence.summary: Initializes Markov chains from the data distribution instead of random values. Biased and may fail to suppress spurious modes. (p. 609)

persistent_cd.label: Persistent CD (PCD) / SML
persistent_cd.summary: Stochastic Maximum Likelihood: Initializes Markov chains from their state in the previous gradient step, allowing them to discover all modes. (p. 612)

fast_pcd.label: Fast PCD
fast_pcd.summary: Uses two sets of parameters (slow and fast weights), where fast weights adapt rapidly to push the Markov chain to new territory. (p. 614)

pseudolikelihood_methods.label: Pseudolikelihood Methods
pseudolikelihood_methods.summary: Training models without Z by using conditional probabilities of features given all others.

pseudolikelihood_objective.label: Pseudolikelihood Objective
pseudolikelihood_objective.summary: The objective is Σ log p(xi | x_{-i}). It is asymptotically consistent. (p. 615)

generalized_pseudolikelihood.label: Generalized Pseudolikelihood
generalized_pseudolikelihood.summary: Uses sets of variables S_i on the left side of the conditioning bar to capture important correlations. (p. 616)

score_matching_methods.label: Score Matching and Ratio Matching
score_matching_methods.summary: Methods that avoid Z by matching derivatives or ratios of the density.

score_matching.label: Score Matching
score_matching.summary: Minimizes the squared difference between the derivatives of the model log-density and the data log-density. Not for discrete data. (p. 617)

ratio_matching.label: Ratio Matching
ratio_matching.summary: Extends score matching to binary data by minimizing the average ratio of probabilities between a state and its 1-bit flip. (p. 618)

denoising_score_matching.label: Denoising Score Matching
denoising_score_matching.summary: Regularized score matching that fits a distribution p_smoothed by adding noise via a corruption process q(x|y). (p. 619)

nce_method.label: Noise-Contrastive Estimation (NCE)
nce_method.summary: Treats the partition function as a parameter c and turns unsupervised density estimation into a binary classification problem between data and noise. (p. 620)

z_estimation.label: Direct Z Estimation
z_estimation.summary: Methods for calculating the value of the partition function for model evaluation.

annealed_importance_sampling.label: Annealed Importance Sampling (AIS)
annealed_importance_sampling.summary: Bridges the gap between a simple proposal p0 and target p1 using a sequence of intermediate distributions. (p. 625)

bridge_sampling.label: Bridge Sampling
bridge_sampling.summary: Uses a single bridge distribution p* to interpolate between p0 and p1, estimating the ratio Z1/Z0. (p. 628)

approximate_inference.label: Approximate Inference
approximate_inference.summary: Techniques for computing the posterior p(h|v) when exact marginalization is intractable.

inference_as_optimization.label: Inference as Optimization
inference_as_optimization.summary: Viewing inference as maximizing a lower bound on the log-likelihood.

elbo.label: Evidence Lower Bound (ELBO)
elbo.summary: L(v, theta, q) = E_q[log p(h,v) - log q(h|v)]. It is the negative variational free energy. (p. 633)

expectation_maximization.label: Expectation Maximization (EM)
expectation_maximization.summary: Iteratively alternates between the E-step (setting q = p(h|v)) and the M-step (maximizing ELBO w.r.t. theta). (p. 634)

map_inference.label: Maximum A Posteriori (MAP) Inference
map_inference.summary: Computing the single most likely value h* = argmax p(h|v), which corresponds to a Dirac distribution q. (p. 635)

sparse_coding_map.label: Sparse Coding MAP
sparse_coding_map.summary: A linear factor model with a Laplace prior; parameters are learned by alternating minimization of the reconstruction error and sparsity penalty. (p. 636)

variational_inference.label: Variational Inference
variational_inference.summary: Maximizing the ELBO over a restricted family of distributions q.

mean_field_approximation.label: Mean Field Approximation
mean_field_approximation.summary: The restriction that q is a factorial distribution: q(h|v) = Π q(hi|v). (p. 638)

calculus_of_variations.label: Calculus of Variations
calculus_of_variations.summary: A mathematical tool for optimizing functionals (functions of functions) by setting functional derivatives to zero. (p. 645)

learned_inference.label: Learned Approximate Inference
learned_inference.summary: Using a neural network to approximate the inference function f: v -> q.

wake_sleep_algorithm.label: Wake-Sleep Algorithm
wake_sleep_algorithm.summary: Trains an inference network by drawing samples from the generative model (sleep) and training the network to predict the latent causes (wake). (p. 651)

variational_autoencoder_inference.label: VAE Inference
variational_autoencoder_inference.summary: An approach where the inference network's parameters are adapted directly to increase the ELBO. (p. 652)

deep_generative_models.label: Deep Generative Models
deep_generative_models.summary: Architectures that represent probability distributions over multiple variables.

bm_energy_function.label: BM Energy Function
bm_energy_function.summary: E(x) = -x^T U x - b^T x, where U is the weight matrix and b is the bias vector. (p. 654)

bm_universal_approximation.label: BM Universal Approximation
bm_universal_approximation.summary: Boltzmann machines with hidden units can act as universal approximators of probability mass functions over discrete variables. (p. 655)

hebbian_learning.label: Hebbian Learning
hebbian_learning.summary: A local learning rule summarized as 'fire together, wire together,' where connections between units that activate together are strengthened. (p. 655)

concept_rbm.label: Restricted Boltzmann Machines (RBMs)
concept_rbm.summary: Undirected probabilistic graphical models consisting of a layer of observable variables and a single layer of latent variables, forming a bipartite graph.

fact_rbm_structure.label: RBM Bipartite Structure
fact_rbm_structure.summary: RBMs are bipartite graphs; no connections are permitted between units within the observed layer or between units within the latent layer. (p 656)

fact_rbm_energy.label: RBM Energy Function
fact_rbm_energy.summary: The joint probability distribution is specified by the energy function E(v, h) = -b^T v - c^T h - v^T W h, where v are visible units, h are hidden units, b and c are bias vectors, and W is the weight matrix. (p 658)

fact_rbm_partition.label: RBM Partition Function
fact_rbm_partition.summary: The normalizing constant Z = sum_{v,h} exp(-E(v,h)) is computationally intractable to evaluate. (p 658)

fact_rbm_conditionals.label: RBM Conditional Distributions
fact_rbm_conditionals.summary: Conditionals P(h|v) and P(v|h) are factorial. P(h_j=1|v) = sigma(c_j + v^T W_{:,j}), where sigma is the sigmoid function. (p 658-659)

fact_rbm_training.label: RBM Training Techniques
fact_rbm_training.summary: RBMs can be trained using Contrastive Divergence (CD), Stochastic Maximum Likelihood (SML/PCD), or ratio matching. (p 659)

concept_dbn.label: Deep Belief Networks (DBNs)
concept_dbn.summary: Hybrid graphical models with several layers of latent variables. Connections between the top two layers are undirected (RBM), while other layers are directed toward the data. (p 659-662)

fact_dbn_structure.label: DBN Architecture
fact_dbn_structure.summary: DBNs contain l hidden layers with weights W(1)...W(l) and biases b(0)...b(l). Visible units can be binary or real. (p 660)

fact_dbn_training.label: DBN Greedy Training
fact_dbn_training.summary: Trained via greedy layer-wise pretraining: each layer is trained as an RBM to model the samples of the previous layer's posterior. (p 661)

fact_dbn_inference.label: DBN Inference Intractability
fact_dbn_inference.summary: Inference is intractable due to the 'explaining away' effect in directed layers and undirected interactions in the top layers. (p 661)

concept_dbm.label: Deep Boltzmann Machines (DBMs)
concept_dbm.summary: Entirely undirected generative models with several layers of latent variables. Like RBMs, they lack intralayer connections. (p 662-675)

fact_dbm_energy.label: DBM Energy Function
fact_dbm_energy.summary: The energy function includes weights between hidden layers: E(v, h1, h2, h3) = -v^T W(1)h1 - h1^T W(2)h2 - h2^T W(3)h3 (biases omitted). (p 663)

fact_dbm_bipartite.label: DBM Bipartite Structure
fact_dbm_bipartite.summary: Layers can be organized into a bipartite graph (odd layers vs even layers). Conditioning on one set makes the other conditionally independent. (p 664)

concept_dbm_inference.label: DBM Mean Field Inference
concept_dbm_inference.summary: Approximate inference using a variational distribution Q that is fully factorial. Optimizes a variational lower bound on log-likelihood. (p 666-668)

fact_dbm_mf_update.label: DBM Mean Field Updates
fact_dbm_mf_update.summary: Fixed point equations: h_hat(1) = sigma(v^T W(1) + h_hat(2)^T W(2)); h_hat(2) = sigma(h_hat(1)^T W(2)). (p 668)

concept_dbm_training.label: DBM Parameter Learning
concept_dbm_training.summary: Trained using Variational SML. Often requires greedy layer-wise pretraining followed by joint training (PCD). (p 668-671)

fact_dbm_centering.label: Centering Trick
fact_dbm_centering.summary: Reparametrizing energy as E'(x; U, b, mu) = -(x-mu)^T U (x-mu) - (x-mu)^T b to improve Hessian conditioning. (p 673)

fact_dbm_mp_dbm.label: Multi-Prediction DBM (MP-DBM)
fact_dbm_mp_dbm.summary: Trained by back-propagating through the inference graph to predict missing input values, avoiding MCMC gradient variance. (p 674-675)

concept_real_val_bm.label: Boltzmann Machines for Real-Valued Data
concept_real_val_bm.summary: Extensions of BMs to handle continuous input variables, often using Gaussian conditional distributions. (p 676-682)

concept_gb_rbm.label: Gaussian-Bernoulli RBMs
concept_gb_rbm.summary: RBMs with real-valued visible units and binary hidden units. P(v|h) is Gaussian. (p 676-677)

fact_gb_energy.label: GB-RBM Energy
fact_gb_energy.summary: Energy function E(v, h) = 1/2 v^T beta v - v^T beta W h - h^T c, where beta is a precision matrix. (p 677)

concept_mc_rbm.label: Mean and Covariance RBM (mcRBM)
concept_mc_rbm.summary: Hidden layer split into mean units (Gaussian RBM) and covariance units (cRBM) to model conditional covariance. (p 678-679)

concept_mpot_rbm.label: Mean-Product of Student's t-distribution (mPoT)
concept_mpot_rbm.summary: Models non-diagonal covariance; conditional distribution over hidden variables is given by independent Gamma distributions. (p 680)

concept_ss_rbm.label: Spike and Slab RBMs (ssRBM)
concept_ss_rbm.summary: Uses binary 'spike' units (h) and real-valued 'slab' units (s) to model covariance without matrix inversion. (p 680-682)

concept_conv_bm.label: Convolutional Boltzmann Machines
concept_conv_bm.summary: RBMs using discrete convolution kernels for translation invariance. (p 683-684)

fact_prob_max_pooling.label: Probabilistic Max Pooling
fact_prob_max_pooling.summary: Constrains detector units so at most one is active; the pooling unit is on if any detector unit is on. (p 683)

concept_struct_bm.label: BMs for Structured/Sequential Outputs
concept_struct_bm.summary: Models mapping input x to output y where y entries are related. (p 685-686)

fact_cond_rbm.label: Conditional RBM
fact_cond_rbm.summary: RBM where bias parameters are a linear function of preceding values in a sequence. (p 685)

fact_rnn_rbm.label: RNN-RBM
fact_rnn_rbm.summary: Generative sequence model where an RNN emits all RBM parameters (including weights) for each time step. (p 686)

concept_stoch_backprop.label: Back-Propagation through Random Operations
concept_stoch_backprop.summary: Methods to compute gradients through stochastic sampling processes. (p 687-691)

concept_reparam_trick.label: Reparametrization Trick
concept_reparam_trick.summary: Expressing a sample y from p(y|theta) as a deterministic function f(z, theta) where z is noise from a fixed distribution. (p 687-688)

fact_reparam_gaussian.label: Gaussian Reparametrization
fact_reparam_gaussian.summary: Sample y ~ N(mu, sigma^2) is rewritten as y = mu + sigma * z, where z ~ N(0, 1). (p 687)

concept_reinforce.label: REINFORCE Algorithm
concept_reinforce.summary: Estimates gradients for discrete stochastic operations using Monte Carlo averaging: grad E[J] approx 1/m sum [ J(y_i) * grad log p(y_i) ]. (p 689-691)

fact_reinforce_baseline.label: REINFORCE Variance Reduction
fact_reinforce_baseline.summary: Using a baseline b(omega) to offset J(y) reduces estimator variance without changing the expectation. (p 690-691)

concept_dir_gen_nets.label: Directed Generative Nets
concept_dir_gen_nets.summary: Fully directed probabilistic models that generate data through ancestral sampling or differentiable functions. (p 692-710)

concept_sbn.label: Sigmoid Belief Networks (SBN)
concept_sbn.summary: Directed models with binary states where each element is influenced by ancestors via sigmoid activations. (p 692-693)

concept_diff_gen_nets.label: Differentiable Generator Networks
concept_diff_gen_nets.summary: Models that transform latent z to x using a differentiable function g(z; theta). (p 693-704)

concept_vae.label: Variational Autoencoders (VAE)
concept_vae.summary: Directed models pairing a generator net (decoder) with an inference net (encoder) to maximize the Variational Lower Bound (ELBO). (p 696-698)

fact_vae_elbo.label: VAE Evidence Lower Bound (ELBO)
fact_vae_elbo.summary: L(q) = E_q[log p(x,z)] - H(q) = E_q[log p(x|z)] - DKL(q(z|x) || p(z)). Consists of reconstruction log-likelihood and a KL divergence term. (p 696)

concept_gan.label: Generative Adversarial Networks (GAN)
concept_gan.summary: A game-theoretic approach where a generator competes against a discriminator to distinguish real from fake data. (p 699-702)

fact_gan_minimax.label: GAN Minimax Objective
fact_gan_minimax.summary: v(G, D) = E_p_data[log D(x)] + E_p_model[log(1 - D(G(z)))]. (p 699)

concept_gmmn.label: Generative Moment Matching Networks (GMMN)
concept_gmmn.summary: Generator nets trained to match statistics (moments) of generated samples to training data using Maximum Mean Discrepancy (MMD). (p 703-704)

concept_auto_reg_nets.label: Auto-Regressive Networks
concept_auto_reg_nets.summary: Directed models with no latent variables that decompose joint probability using the chain rule: P(x) = Product P(x_i | x_{<i}). (p 705-710)

fact_nade_sharing.label: NADE Weight Sharing
fact_nade_sharing.summary: Neural Auto-Regressive Density Estimator shares weights between groups of hidden units to reduce parameters and computation. (p 708-709)

concept_ae_sampling.label: Drawing Samples from Autoencoders
concept_ae_sampling.summary: Techniques to generate samples from models that do not explicitly define a joint distribution, such as Denoising Autoencoders. (p 711-715)

concept_gsn.label: Generative Stochastic Networks (GSN)
concept_gsn.summary: Generalizations of denoising autoencoders that include latent variables in a generative Markov chain. (p 714-715)

concept_eval_gen_models.label: Evaluating Generative Models
concept_eval_gen_models.summary: Methodologies and challenges in comparing generative models, including log-likelihood, visual inspection, and AIS. (p 717-718)

fact_eval_likelihood_issues.label: Log-Likelihood Evaluation Pitfalls
fact_eval_likelihood_issues.summary: Real-valued models on MNIST can achieve infinite likelihood by assigning near-zero variance to constant background pixels. (p 718)

model_objectives.label: Model Objectives and Metrics
model_objectives.summary: The goals of generative modeling and the methods used to measure their success, emphasizing that metrics must align with the intended use case.

probability_assignment.label: Probability Assignment Strategies
probability_assignment.summary: Different generative models prioritize different types of probability assignments based on their design.

fact_realistic_points.label: High Probability for Realistic Points
fact_realistic_points.summary: Some generative models are optimized to assign high probability to most realistic data points.

fact_unrealistic_points.label: Low Probability for Unrealistic Points
fact_unrealistic_points.summary: Other generative models are optimized to rarely assign high probability to unrealistic points.

divergence_metrics.label: Divergence Metrics
divergence_metrics.summary: Mathematical measures used to quantify the difference between the data distribution and the model distribution.

fact_kl_divergence_direction.label: KL Divergence Directionality
fact_kl_divergence_direction.summary: Differences in model behavior (e.g., focus on realistic vs. unrealistic points) result from whether the model minimizes D KL(pdata || pmodel) or D KL(pmodel || pdata).

probabilistic_modeling.label: Probabilistic Modeling
probabilistic_modeling.summary: The formulation of generative models as probability distributions over inputs and latent variables.

fact_model_distributions.label: Model and Representation Distributions
fact_model_distributions.summary: Generative models learn a model pmodel(x) and a representation pmodel(h | x) to understand the world represented in training data.

hierarchical_representation.label: Hierarchical Representation
hierarchical_representation.summary: The organization of latent variables (h) into layers to capture different levels of abstraction.

fact_expectation_layers.label: Expectations Across Layers
fact_expectation_layers.summary: A generative model can provide different ways of representing x by taking expectations of h at different layers of the hierarchy.

model_architectures.label: Model Architectures
model_architectures.summary: The technical frameworks used to implement deep generative models, as evidenced by domain literature.

energy_based_models.label: Energy-Based Models (EBMs)
energy_based_models.summary: Models that define a probability distribution via an energy function.

restricted_boltzmann_machines.label: Restricted Boltzmann Machines (RBMs)
restricted_boltzmann_machines.summary: A type of EBM with a bipartite graph structure between visible and hidden units.

deep_boltzmann_machines.label: Deep Boltzmann Machines (DBMs)
deep_boltzmann_machines.summary: Hierarchical extensions of RBMs with multiple layers of hidden units.

adversarial_models.label: Adversarial Models
adversarial_models.summary: Models that use a game-theoretic approach to generate data.

generative_adversarial_networks.label: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs)
generative_adversarial_networks.summary: Models consisting of a generator and a discriminator competing in a zero-sum game.

variational_models.label: Variational Models
variational_models.summary: Models that use variational inference to approximate intractable posterior distributions.

variational_autoencoders.label: Variational Autoencoders (VAEs)
variational_autoencoders.summary: Autoencoders that learn a latent distribution rather than a fixed point encoding.

stochastic_networks.label: Generative Stochastic Networks (GSNs)
stochastic_networks.summary: Networks designed to model data generating distributions using stochastic units.

inference_and_reasoning.label: Inference and Reasoning
inference_and_reasoning.summary: The application of generative models to solve problems and draw conclusions about input data.

relationship_inference.label: Relationship Inference
relationship_inference.summary: Using the learned model to uncover dependencies between variables.

fact_input_variable_relationships.label: Input Variable Relationships
fact_input_variable_relationships.summary: Generative models can provide answers to many inference problems regarding the relationships between input variables in x.

uncertainty_reasoning.label: Reasoning Under Uncertainty
uncertainty_reasoning.summary: The ability of AI systems to apply intuitive concepts and reason despite incomplete or noisy data.

fact_uncertainty_framework.label: Framework for Intuitive Concepts
fact_uncertainty_framework.summary: Generative models provide AI systems with a framework for intuitive concepts and the ability to reason about them in the face of uncertainty.

neural_architectures.label: Neural Architectures
neural_architectures.summary: The structural organization of artificial neurons and layers to process information.

feedforward_networks.label: Feedforward Networks
feedforward_networks.summary: Networks where connections do not form cycles, passing information in one direction.

mlp.label: Multilayer Perceptron (MLP)
mlp.summary: A class of feedforward artificial neural network consisting of at least three layers of nodes: an input layer, a hidden layer, and an output layer.

perceptron.label: Perceptron
perceptron.summary: The basic unit of a neural network, a linear classifier.

recurrent_networks.label: Recurrent Networks
recurrent_networks.summary: Networks with feedback loops allowing information to persist, suitable for sequential data.

tdnn.label: Time-Delay Neural Network (TDNN)
tdnn.summary: A network architecture designed to handle time-series data by incorporating delays.

stochastic_generative_models.label: Stochastic Generative Models
stochastic_generative_models.summary: Models that learn the probability distribution of the data to generate new samples.

ssrbm.label: Spike and Slab RBM
ssrbm.summary: A variation of the RBM incorporating spike and slab priors for sparsity.

dbm.label: Deep Boltzmann Machine (DBM)
dbm.summary: A multi-layer extension of the RBM.

vae.label: Variational Autoencoder (VAE)
vae.summary: A generative model that learns a latent representation of data using variational inference.

specialized_architectures.label: Specialized Architectures
specialized_architectures.summary: Architectures tailored for specific data types or tasks.

pooling.label: Pooling
pooling.summary: A down-sampling operation to reduce spatial dimensions.

separable_convolution.label: Separable Convolution
separable_convolution.summary: A technique to decompose a standard convolution into smaller, more efficient operations.

ntm.label: Neural Turing Machine (NTM)
ntm.summary: A neural network architecture that combines neural networks with an external memory bank.

spn.label: Sum-Product Network (SPN)
spn.summary: A deep probabilistic model that represents a joint distribution as a computation graph.

regression.label: Regression
regression.summary: A task of predicting a continuous value.

reinforcement_learning.label: Reinforcement Learning
reinforcement_learning.summary: Learning to make decisions by performing actions in an environment to maximize a reward.

reinforce_algorithm.label: REINFORCE
reinforce_algorithm.summary: A policy gradient method in reinforcement learning.

advanced_learning_strategies.label: Advanced Learning Strategies
advanced_learning_strategies.summary: Specialized learning methods for complex data or constraints.

transfer_learning.label: Transfer Learning
transfer_learning.summary: Applying knowledge learned from one task to a different but related task.

one_shot_learning.label: One-Shot Learning
one_shot_learning.summary: Learning to recognize a category from only one training example.

zero_shot_learning.label: Zero-Shot Learning
zero_shot_learning.summary: Recognizing categories that the model has never seen during training.

multi_modal_learning.label: Multi-modal Learning
multi_modal_learning.summary: Learning from multiple types of data (e.g., text and images).

optimization_regularization.label: Optimization and Regularization
optimization_regularization.summary: Techniques for training models and preventing overfitting.

gradient_based_optimization.label: Gradient-Based Optimization
gradient_based_optimization.summary: Algorithms that use the gradient of the objective function to update weights.

sgd.label: Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD)
sgd.summary: An iterative method for optimizing an objective function with randomly chosen subsets of training data.

second_order_optimization.label: Second-Order Optimization
second_order_optimization.summary: Algorithms using Hessian matrices (second derivatives) to improve convergence speed.

quasi_newton.label: Quasi-Newton Methods
quasi_newton.summary: Approximations of Newton's method that avoid computing the full Hessian matrix.

regularization_techniques.label: Regularization Techniques
regularization_techniques.summary: Methods to reduce overfitting by penalizing model complexity.

weight_decay.label: Weight Decay
weight_decay.summary: L2 regularization that penalizes large weights to prevent overfitting.

regularizer_general.label: Regularizer
regularizer_general.summary: A term added to the loss function to constrain the model's parameters.

probability_distributions.label: Probability Distributions
probability_distributions.summary: Mathematical functions that describe the likelihood of different outcomes.

normal_distribution.label: Normal (Gaussian) Distribution
normal_distribution.summary: A continuous probability distribution characterized by a bell curve.

multinomial_distribution.label: Multinomial Distribution
multinomial_distribution.summary: A generalization of the binomial distribution to multiple possible outcomes.

probabilistic_methods.label: Probabilistic Methods
probabilistic_methods.summary: Approaches for estimating parameters and likelihoods.

naive_bayes.label: Naive Bayes
naive_bayes.summary: A simple probabilistic classifier based on Bayes' theorem with strong independence assumptions.

pseudolikelihood.label: Pseudolikelihood
pseudolikelihood.summary: An approximation used for training graphical models where the full likelihood is computationally intractable.

information_theory.label: Information Theory
information_theory.summary: The mathematical study of the quantification, storage, and communication of information.

self_information.label: Self-information
self_information.summary: The amount of information gained when a specific outcome occurs.

mathematical_foundations.label: Mathematical Foundations
mathematical_foundations.summary: The underlying mathematics required for machine learning.

svd.label: Singular Value Decomposition (SVD)
svd.summary: A factorization of a matrix into three constituent matrices, used for dimensionality reduction.

orthogonal_matrix.label: Orthogonal Matrix
orthogonal_matrix.summary: A square matrix whose columns and rows are orthogonal unit vectors.

norms.label: Norm
norms.summary: A function that assigns a strictly positive length or size to each vector in a vector space.

partial_derivative.label: Partial Derivative
partial_derivative.summary: The derivative of a multi-variable function with respect to one variable while others are held constant.

second_derivative.label: Second Derivative
second_derivative.summary: The derivative of the derivative of a function, indicating curvature.

statistics.label: Statistics
statistics.summary: The science of collecting, analyzing, interpreting, and presenting data.

point_estimator.label: Point Estimator
point_estimator.summary: A single-value estimate of a population parameter.

statistical_learning_theory.label: Statistical Learning Theory
statistical_learning_theory.summary: A framework for analyzing the performance of machine learning algorithms.

application_domains.label: Application Domains
application_domains.summary: Specific fields where machine learning is applied.

ngram.label: n-gram
ngram.summary: A contiguous sequence of n items from a given sample of text.

word_embedding.label: Word Embedding
word_embedding.summary: Representing words as dense vectors in a continuous vector space.

computer_vision.label: Computer Vision
computer_vision.summary: Training computers to interpret and understand the visual world.

object_detection.label: Object Detection
object_detection.summary: Identifying and locating objects within an image.

object_recognition.label: Object Recognition
object_recognition.summary: Classifying an object as belonging to a specific category.

recommender_systems.label: Recommender Systems
recommender_systems.summary: Algorithms designed to suggest relevant items to users.
